While under the effects of this Charm, the character can perceive incorporeal spirits as though they had manifested, although they remain invisible to others. Additionally, the character may scrutinize a target's aura as a simple action by spending 1 mote and his player rolling Perception + Martial Arts. Each success on this roll gauges one of the target's following Traits as decided by the observer's player: health levels remaining, permanent Essence rating or total current Essence pool. This Charm cannot discern the nature of a magical being, only its overall power. Thus, characters cannot determine the type or caste of an Exalted or differentiate between Personal and Peripheral Essence without other magic.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Martial Arts tree, p. 163 (PDF 164). Tree diagram confirmed on p. 165 (PDF 166): a single linear-branching tree rooted here, not two separate trees as with Brawl.

name: Shrouded Claw Attack
summary: Suffuses the Abyssal's hands with the spectral Essence of the Underworld, making unarmed strikes flicker like the blows of a ghost and halving an opponent's defensive dice pool.
requirements: Minimum Martial Arts 2; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Essence Discerning Glance.
mechanics: The character suffuses her hands with the spectral Essence of the Underworld, causing them to flicker like the corpus of a ghost. As a result, players of characters attempting to dodge or parry blows enhanced with this Charm roll only half the character's normal dice pool, rounded down. In addition, such attacks make no noise, even from impact. The Essence to power this Charm must be spent prior to making the attack roll. This Charm is not compatible with the use of weapons.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Martial Arts tree, p. 163 (PDF 164).

name: Hungry Ghost Form
summary: Transforms the Abyssal into the visage of a ravening shade with pallid, faintly translucent flesh, granting lethal unarmed damage, Essence drain from harming the animate, and the ability to strike incorporeal spirits.
requirements: Minimum Martial Arts 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Shrouded Claw Attack.
mechanics: The Exalted takes on the visage and attitude of a ravening shade, his pallid flesh growing cold and faintly translucent as he coils to lunge. For the rest of the scene, the character inflicts lethal damage with all hand-to-hand attacks. Additionally, he regains 1 mote of Essence for every health level of damage inflicted against animate targets (living creatures, spirits, undead, etc.). Lastly, the character may reflexively spend 3 motes per attack to strike dematerialized spirits, although this Charm provides no ability to perceive such beings. Spirits slain by this Charm eventually regenerate unless other magic is employed, but this process takes time and is extremely painful. Characters cannot use more than one Martial Arts Form-type Charm at a time. This Charm is incompatible with the use of armor.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Martial Arts tree, p. 163 (PDF 164).

name: Power Reaping Prana
summary: Executing quick slashes in the air, the Abyssal reaches forth her anima to siphon up Essence as it flows from her enemies, draining an opponent's Combo before it can take effect.
requirements: Minimum Martial Arts 4; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Hungry Ghost Form.
mechanics: Executing a series of quick slashes in the air, the Exalt reaches forth her anima to siphon up expended Essence as it flows from her enemies. In order to use this Charm, the character must already have Essence Discerning Glance active and her target must be within 10 yards when spending Essence to power an effect. For the purposes of this Charm, the total Essence cost of all Charms in a Combo is considered one effect. The character's player rolls Perception + Martial Arts; each success allows the Exalt to regain 2 motes of Essence. The character may not gain more Essence from a single trigger than the total motes spent powering it, so a character that achieves three successes draining a Charm costing 4 motes only gains 4 motes rather than 6. Use of this Charm does not in any way disrupt the effect being drained. At the end of the turn, all remaining motes acquired via this Charm in excess of the character's permanent Essence dissipate. This limit applies regardless of how many times this Charm is activated in a turn. Power Reaping Prana is explicitly permitted to be part of a Combo with Charms of other Abilities.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Martial Arts tree, pp. 163-164 (PDF 164-165). Effect text spans the page break.

name: Charm Smothering Technique
summary: Lashing out with soul-numbing power, the Abyssal stifles an enemy's magic before it takes form, countering singular Charms activated within 10 yards unless the target pays a steep Essence surcharge.
requirements: Minimum Martial Arts 5; Minimum Essence 4; Prerequisite Charms: Power Reaping Prana.
mechanics: Lashing out with a soul-numbing tendril of power, the Exalt stifles her enemy's magic before it even takes form. Charms aborted in this fashion manifest as a burst of dimly glowing sparks that do not contribute to the victim's anima banner. Abyssal characters must have Essence Discerning Glance active in order to perceive the use of Charms before they take effect, although the deathknights do not know which Charms are being used until their players make a successful reflexive Intelligence + Occult roll (difficulty 2). Similarly, Charm Smothering Technique can only counter Charms activated within 10 yards of the Exalt. Targets of this Charm may immediately spend a number of additional motes equal to the Essence invested by the Abyssal. If they cannot or do not pay this surcharge, their Charms fail, and all costs spent on the stillborn magic are lost. If the target pays the surcharge, the Charm takes effect normally. Charm Smothering Technique can only counter singular Charms -- Combos, spells, Fair Folk glamour and other forms of magic cannot be smothered. Characters cannot spend more motes on this Charm than their Wits + Martial Arts, nor can they use Power Reaping Prana to draw energy from smothered Charms.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Martial Arts tree, p. 164 (PDF 165).

name: Consuming Entropy Strike
summary: Wreathes the Abyssal's hand in a crackling nimbus of Oblivion that inflicts normal lethal damage while also permanently eroding the target's soak for the duration of the single attack.
requirements: Minimum Martial Arts 5; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Hungry Ghost Form.
mechanics: The character brings to bear the ravaging power of Oblivion in a crackling nimbus around her hand. In addition to inflicting lethal damage, the character's attack reduces the target's soak by 2L per mote spent. A target's soak cannot be reduced below zero. This reduced soak only applies to resisting this single attack, and returns to normal immediately thereafter. Weakening non-magical armor with this Charm leaves a fine layer of rust or rot at the point of impact, although this decay is too minor to damage the armor.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Martial Arts tree, pp. 164-165 (PDF 165-166); cost/header block on p. 164 (PDF 165), effect text continues onto p. 165 (PDF 166).

name: Blood Freezing Technique
summary: The Abyssal's fingers rigidify into claws that inflict a bitter, dexterity-numbing cold, freezing a victim toward total paralysis on a strong hit.
requirements: Minimum Martial Arts 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Consuming Entropy Strike.
mechanics: The character's fingers tighten in rigid claws, and his skin becomes numbingly cold to the touch. In addition to inflicting lethal damage, his attack drains warmth on impact. If the attack inflicts damage, the target loses one dot of Dexterity. Recalculate the victim's initiative accordingly and apply this new rating immediately. Characters who have not yet acted on the turn in which they are numbed have their actions delayed until their new initiative total. Lost Dexterity returns at the end of the scene (or in 10 to 15 minutes in the case of long scenes). Characters reduced to zero Dexterity are paralyzed and can take no physical action, although they can still clearly think and are allowed by their wound penalties and combat Charms that do not require movement. Blood Freezing Technique has no effect on beings immune to cold, including most undead and automata.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Martial Arts tree, p. 165 (PDF 166). Text uses 'Supplementary' rather than the usual 'Supplemental' type label for this entry; transcribed as printed.

name: Unnatural Shambling Deftness
summary: The Abyssal's motions take on the unsettling jerkiness of the walking dead, granting extra combat-related actions at the cost of no longer being able to split her dice pool.
requirements: Minimum Martial Arts 5; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Hungry Ghost Form.
mechanics: The character's motions take on the unsettling jerkiness of the walking dead as she wavers between impossible bursts of speed and total stillness. The character may take a total number of extra actions equal to her permanent Essence. These actions can be used for any combat-related tasks, subject to Storyteller approval. The character cannot split her dice pool on the same turn she employs this Charm. This Charm is incompatible with the use of armor.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Martial Arts tree, p. 165 (PDF 166). Named 'Unnatural Shambling Defense' on the tree diagram on p. 165/PDF 166, but the body text and header both use 'Unnatural Shambling Deftness'; the body-text name is treated as authoritative.

name: Lunging Phantom Method
summary: The Abyssal rushes forward, twisting and dematerializing as he passes through an enemy, then rematerializes behind them to strike with the benefits of a rear attack.
requirements: Minimum Martial Arts 2; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Unnatural Shambling Deftness.
mechanics: The Abyssal rushes forward, twisting and dematerializing as he passes through his enemy, and rematerializing behind her. The subsequent attack does no more damage than usual, but it gains all of the benefits of attacking from behind (per core Exalted's rear-attack rules). This Charm is incompatible with the use of armor.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Martial Arts tree, p. 165 (PDF 166). Flagged for re-verification: printed Minimum Martial Arts of 2 is unusually low for a Charm this deep in the prerequisite chain (its own prerequisite, Unnatural Shambling Deftness, requires Martial Arts 5); re-check against a higher-zoom render before promotion in case this is a misprint or a misread digit. Cross-references core Exalted p. 238 for the rear-attack bonus.

name: Soul-Flaying Strike
summary: Capstone of the Dusk Caste Martial Arts tree; a powerful open-handed blow crackling with the Abyssal's anima that inflicts unsoakable aggravated damage rolled against the victim's own Essence, raising most slain victims as hungry ghosts.
requirements: Minimum Martial Arts 5; Minimum Essence 4; Prerequisite Charms: Charm Smothering Technique, Blood Freezing Technique, Lunging Phantom Method.
mechanics: The deathknight delivers a powerful open-handed blow, Essence crackling around his clawed fingers in moaning arcs. The character makes the attack as normal. If the strike hits, roll the Abyssal's permanent Essence against the permanent Essence of the victim. If the Exalt wins, the victim suffers unsoakable aggravated damage equal to the deathknight's Martial Arts score (damage dice are rolled normally). This damage is in addition to any inflicted by the actual strike. Victims slain by this Charm arise as hungry ghosts upon the next sunset. Such ghosts have the usual statistics for their kind (see p. 127) but are never extras, and they obey the Abyssal to the best of their limited intelligence. Spirits and Fair Folk slain with this Charm are annihilated utterly and evaporate on the spot. This Charm is incompatible with the use of armor.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Martial Arts tree, p. 165 (PDF 166). Cross-references p. 127 of this book for hungry ghost statistics, a page not yet inventoried here.

name: Furious Blade
summary: Root Charm of the Dusk Caste Melee tree; envelops the Abyssal's weapon in a corona of roiling darkness with predatory zeal, letting her add extra dice to a single attack.
requirements: Minimum Melee 1; Minimum Essence 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: Enveloped in a corona of roiling darkness, the Abyssal's weapon moves with predatory zeal to cut down enemies. The character may add one die to a single attack for every mote spent but cannot more than double his Dexterity + Melee dice pool.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Melee tree, p. 165 (PDF 166). Opens the Melee section immediately after the end of Martial Arts.

name: Savage Shade Style
summary: Channels fury and Essence through the Abyssal's weapon to deliver horrible rending blows, doubling the value of extra successes toward damage.
requirements: Minimum Melee 2; Minimum Essence 1; Prerequisite Charms: Furious Blade.
mechanics: With this Charm, the Abyssal focuses fury and Essence through his weapon to inflict horrible rending blows. The character makes his attack as normal, but successes count twice for the purposes of determining damage. This Charm must be invoked before making the attack roll.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Melee tree ('Melee 1'), p. 166 (PDF 167).

name: Artful Maiming Onslaught
summary: Aims a strike with cruel precision to sever limbs and mutilate an opponent, capping damage at the minimum needed for the maiming rather than the full damage roll.
requirements: Minimum Melee 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Savage Shade Style.
mechanics: Striking with cruel precision, an Abyssal with this Charm aims his blow to sever limbs and mutilate his opponent. Add the Abyssal's Dexterity to the damage of his attack, but this attack has a difficulty of at least 3. Severing an arm or leg (or tentacle or similarly sized appendage) is difficulty 3 and requires the Exalt to inflict at least two health levels of damage after soak. Severing a hand or putting out an eye increases the attack difficulty to 4 but only requires a single level of damage. Regardless of the actual damage rolled, the Abyssal's strike only inflicts the minimum health levels necessary for the maiming. Thus, a character who rolls five health levels of damage after the target's soak only inflicts two levels on an attempt to sever an arm. Victims still must contend with bleeding and shock, however. Consider the amputee's wound penalty to be twice its usual value until her bleeding is stanched. Additionally, victims' players must make a reflexive Stamina + Resistance roll for their characters to take any action on the turn they lose a limb.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Melee tree ('Melee 1'), p. 166 (PDF 167). Cross-references core Exalted p. 234 for maiming-related restrictions/penalties.

name: Slashing Ghost Talon
summary: The Abyssal's blade shrieks and moans as it becomes a conduit for her insatiable hunger, regaining Essence for every health level of damage inflicted, doubled with a soulsteel weapon.
requirements: Minimum Melee 2; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Furious Blade.
mechanics: The character's blade shrieks and moans as it becomes a conduit for her insatiable hunger. The deathknight makes her attack as normal but regains 1 mote of Essence for every health level of damage inflicted. If the Abyssal uses a soulsteel weapon to strike a being with an Essence pool, she also absorbs the motes stolen by her weapon. This latter bonus only applies if the character is attuned to her weapon.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Melee tree ('Melee 1'), pp. 166-167 (PDF 167-168); effect text continues onto the following page.

name: Crimson Banquet Method
summary: Harvests power from every blow that draws blood for a full scene, duplicating Slashing Ghost Talon's Essence-drain but limited by the Abyssal's Conviction.
requirements: Minimum Melee 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Slashing Ghost Talon.
mechanics: With this Charm, the character harvests power from every blow that draws blood. Crimson Banquet Method duplicates the effects of Slashing Ghost Talon, but the bonus applies to every attack made during the scene. This Charm cannot be stacked with itself to gain multiple motes per health level inflicted, nor may the Abyssal use Slashing Ghost Talon while employing this Charm. A character cannot gain more Essence in a single turn from the use of this Charm than the character's Essence + Lore.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Melee tree ('Melee 1'), p. 167 (PDF 168).

name: Reaper of Men
summary: Suffuses the Abyssal's body and weapon with a nimbus of baleful energy for a scene, giving hand-to-hand and hand-and-weapon attacks lethal damage and Essence drain and compelling mindless dead to fear the character.
requirements: Minimum Melee 5; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Crimson Banquet Method.
mechanics: The deathknight suffuses her body and weapon with a nimbus of baleful energy, wreathing herself in a necrotic corona. Any living being who touches her or strikes her with a hand-to-hand attack suffers lethal damage equal to the Abyssal's Essence rating. The character's hand-to-hand attacks also inflict lethal damage and add her Essence to the damage of the attack. Mindless ghosts and walking dead fear characters using this Charm and will not attack them unless mystically compelled.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Melee tree ('Melee 1'), p. 167 (PDF 168).

name: Soul-Searing Blow
summary: Projects the spiritual cold of Oblivion through the Abyssal's weapon to assault a foe's soul, draining temporary Willpower whether or not the attack inflicts physical damage.
requirements: Minimum Melee 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Slashing Ghost Talon.
mechanics: Projecting the spiritual cold of Oblivion through his weapon, the Abyssal can assault the very soul and will of a foe. If the character's attack hits (it need not inflict damage), the victim loses 1 point of temporary Willpower for every 2 motes spent. Exalted and other beings with control over their Essence pools may choose to lose 2 motes of Essence for every Willpower point they would have otherwise lost. If this Charm reduces a character's temporary Willpower below zero, she suffers unsoakable lethal damage equal to the difference. Thus, a victim with 3 Willpower remaining who loses 5 points takes 2L damage. This damage is soaked only with the character's permanent Essence score and nothing else. The Abyssal cannot spend more motes powering this Charm than twice her Conviction.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Melee tree ('Melee 1'), p. 167 (PDF 168).

name: Soul-Cleaving Strike
summary: Capstone of the first Dusk Caste Melee tree; the greatest swordsmen of the Underworld can slice through souls as easily as flesh, threatening total, permanent Essence-draining annihilation.
requirements: Minimum Melee 5; Minimum Essence 4; Prerequisite Charms: Reaper of Men, Soul-Searing Blow.
mechanics: The greatest swordsmen of the deathknights can slice through souls as easily as others carve flesh. Upon invoking this Charm, the Abyssal's weapon flares with cold fire and shrieks loud enough to be heard up to a mile away. The character makes one attack at his full dice pool, which is fully effective against both material beings and incorporeal spirits and does normal damage in addition to this Charm's effects. If the blow hits, the victim's player must immediately roll permanent Essence at standard difficulty. If this roll succeeds, the victim suffers unsoakable loss of lethal damage equal to the difference between the Abyssal's own Essence rating and the roll. If the roll fails, the victim loses one dot of permanent Essence and damage. A botch inflicts permanent Essence loss and damage. If a character's permanent Essence drops to zero, her life force is instantly snuffed out, and her maimed soul falls screaming into Oblivion. Spirits and Fair Folk slain in this manner are likewise destroyed. Damage inflicted by Soul-Cleaving Strike is purely spiritual and cannot be soaked or prevented with magic that solely defends against physical assault. All effects of this Charm are applied before resolving the strike's normal damage. This Charm does not work on automata, the walking dead or other beings without souls.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Melee tree ('Melee 1'), p. 168 (PDF 169). Effect text as transcribed conflates two distinct failure conditions (roll succeeds vs. roll fails); flagged for re-verification of the exact success/failure wording against a higher-zoom render before promotion.

name: Five Shadow Feint
summary: The Abyssal's arm and weapon flicker into a confusing spray of shadows and afterimages, letting her spend Essence to strip a defender's dice pool at the cost of her own attack pool being similarly capped.
requirements: Minimum Melee 2; Minimum Essence 1; Prerequisite Charms: Furious Blade.
mechanics: The Abyssal's arm and weapon flickers, blossoming into a confusing spray of shadows and afterimages. The character makes his attack normally, but the target loses one die from her first defensive dice pool for every mote spent. The Abyssal may not reduce a character's dice pool below her Essence rating. If Five Shadow Feint is placed in a Combo with Furious Blade, the Essence cost of both Charms increases to 2 motes per die.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Melee tree ('Melee 1'), p. 167 (PDF 168).

name: Ebon Lightning Prana
summary: Drawing a blade and lunging in a single fluid motion, an Abyssal with this Charm strikes faster than mortal eyes can follow, suffering no initiative penalty for drawing a sheathed weapon.
requirements: Minimum Melee 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Five Shadow Feint.
mechanics: Drawing his blade and lunging in a single fluid motion, an Abyssal with this Charm can strike faster than mortal eyes can follow. The character suffers no penalty for drawing a sheathed weapon and strikes whenever he wishes without regard for initiative. Although his first action must be a Melee attack, he can still split his dice pool normally to take other actions later in the turn. However, the character cannot take any actions after the first attack until his regular initiative. If the character faces an opponent with similar magic, normal initiative determines who acts first. A character can only use Ebon Lightning Prana once per turn, and in order to use it, the weapon must be sheathed. For the purposes of this Charm, sheathing a sword requires no roll, but is counted as one of the character's actions for the turn.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Melee tree ('Melee 1'), p. 168 (PDF 169).

name: Unfurling Iron Lotus
summary: The Abyssal spins and thrusts in a rapid cascade of blows resembling the petals of a blooming flower, gaining additional full-pool attacks limited only by her Essence.
requirements: Minimum Melee 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Five Shadow Feint.
mechanics: The Abyssal spins and thrusts in a rapid cascade of blows. The Charm takes its name from the wispy contrails left by each strike, which, taken together, resemble the petals of a blooming flower. The character may make one additional attack at his full dice pool for every 3 motes spent, although he may not purchase more extra attacks than his Essence score. Characters must activate this Charm before taking their first action and may not split their dice pool on the same turn they employ Unfurling Iron Lotus. Defenders must dodge or parry each attack separately.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Melee tree ('Melee 1'), p. 168 (PDF 169).

name: Glorious Carnage Typhoon
summary: Capstone of blade-flashing carnage in a spiral of blood and pain and death; the Abyssal scythes through opponents like a tornado, automatically continuing to a new victim with every hit until her blade finds no more targets within reach.
requirements: Minimum Melee 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Unfurling Iron Lotus.
mechanics: Blade flashing in a spiral of blood and pain and death, the Abyssal scythes through her opponents like a tornado. So long as the character hits her intended target and inflicts damage, she may immediately make another attack at her full dice pool against a different victim at her full dice pool. Each attack must be leveled at a different victim, and the Exalt can move more yards than her Melee score between each target. This Charm ends when the character misses or strikes every victim within reach of her blade.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Melee tree ('Melee 1'), p. 168 (PDF 169).

name: Blade-Summoning Gesture
summary: Root of the second Dusk Caste Melee tree; extends the Abyssal's will and anima in a grasping tendril to call a previously wielded weapon to her hand from anywhere in sight.
requirements: Minimum Melee 2; Minimum Essence 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: Extending his will and anima in a grasping tendril, the Abyssal calls his weapon to his hand. Summoned weapons can overcome friction and gravity -- even pull free from bodies -- but cannot defeat walls, chains or similar obstacles. The character must be able to see his weapon and have a hand free to receive it. Furthermore, this Charm can only call weapons the Exalt has previously wielded.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Melee tree ('Melee 2'), p. 168 (PDF 169).

name: Thieving Raiton Claws
summary: A variant use of Blade-Summoning Gesture that lets the Abyssal steal a foe's weapon instead of retrieving her own, tearing it from the enemy's grasp with a contested Dexterity + Melee roll.
requirements: Minimum Melee 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Blade-Summoning Gesture.
mechanics: Instead of retrieving her own weapon, an Abyssal with Thieving Raiton Claws may attempt to steal the weapon of a foe. The Exalt reaches out an empty hand, and her player rolls Dexterity + Melee at difficulty 3. This effect cannot be parried or dodged. If this roll is successful, the effect is resolved as a normal disarming attempt. If the disarming succeeds, the targeted weapon is torn from the enemy's grasp and flies to the Abyssal's own. This Charm can steal any weapon in the character's line of sight, although it cannot seize magical weapons attuned to their wielders or weapons made entirely of Essence. Otherwise, this Charm duplicates the effects and limitations of Blade-Summoning Gesture.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Melee tree ('Melee 2'), p. 169 (PDF 170). Cross-references core Exalted p. 238 for the base disarming attempt it resolves against.

name: Void Sheath Technique
summary: Banishes a familiar weapon from the world entirely into a hidden Elsewhere, ready to be drawn back forth with a thought at any time.
requirements: Minimum Melee 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Blade-Summoning Gesture.
mechanics: With a moment's concentration, an Abyssal who knows this Charm may banish a weapon from his grasp and the world. The weapon shimmers and vanishes, remaining hidden and inaccessible until the character reflexively ends the Charm and draws his weapon forth. This Charm can only banish a single weapon at a time, one the Abyssal is intimately familiar with -- typically his most prized implement of battle.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Melee tree ('Melee 2'), p. 169 (PDF 170).

name: Resplendent Shadow Blade
summary: Capstone of the second Dusk Caste Melee tree; raising her hand imperiously, the Abyssal freezes raw Essence into an ideal weapon of black crystal that always summons the same blade once its form is chosen.
requirements: Minimum Melee 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Void Sheath Technique.
mechanics: Raising her hand imperiously, a deathknight with this Charm freezes raw Essence into her ideal weapon. This weapon appears sculpted of black crystal and glitters with power and malice. Although most deathknights prefer variations of slashing swords, this Charm can create any bladed weapon from ornate scythes to jagged tiger claws. When Resplendent Shadow Blade is purchased, the Abyssal's player must decide the form of the weapon. He then divides a number of points equal to twice the character's Melee score between the weapon's Speed, Damage, Accuracy and Defense. As usual, the damage bonus of the weapon is added to the character's Strength to determine its lethal damage. Once selected, this Charm always summons the same weapon; the blade's statistics remain constant unless the character raises his Melee score, permitting him to divide two more points to its characteristics. The Abyssal may purchase this Charm again to conjure a different form of blade. Weapons created with this Charm have the tensile strength of soulsteel -- and likewise drain motes equal to their owner's permanent Essence on any hit that inflicts actual damage.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Melee tree ('Melee 2'), p. 169 (PDF 170).

name: Elegant Flowing Deflection
summary: Root of the third, defense-focused Dusk Caste Melee tree; the Exalt moves with preternatural grace, parrying incoming hand-to-hand attacks she is aware of without breaking form or stride.
requirements: Minimum Melee 1; Minimum Essence 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: The Exalt moves with preternatural grace, shifting his weapon without breaking form or stride to parry any hand-to-hand attack he is aware of. The character's player rolls two dice for every mote spent but cannot purchase more dice than his normal defensive pool for the weapon. This total includes applicable specialties and weapon bonuses in addition to the character's Dexterity + Melee. If the character has an odd number of dice in his pool after buying extra dice, the fractional mote remaining after buying is lost.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Melee tree ('Melee 3'), p. 170 (PDF 171).

name: Vengeful Riposte
summary: Shifting quickly from defense to offense, the character parries an incoming strike with a swift blow to the attacker's weapon hand or limb, converting leftover parry successes into a counterattack.
requirements: Minimum Melee 2; Minimum Essence 1; Prerequisite Charms: Elegant Flowing Deflection.
mechanics: Shifting quickly from defense to offense, the character parries the attacker's weapon hand or limb with a swift blow. If the character's player rolls more successes than the attacker, any leftover successes are treated as a Melee attack against the aggressor. Thus, a parry that rolls five successes to deflect an attack with three successes becomes a two-success attack. This counterstrike cannot be blocked or dodged without magic. A character may not use Vengeful Riposte in response to other counterattack Charms. Note that this Charm does not grant the character a free parry or extra dice.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Melee tree ('Melee 3'), p. 170 (PDF 171).

name: Corrosive Parry
summary: Fills the Abyssal's blade with necrotic Essence as she parries, corroding an opponent's weapon to dust or splinters on even a single success against a close-range attack.
requirements: Minimum Melee 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Vengeful Riposte.
mechanics: Filling his blade with necrotic Essence as he parries, the Abyssal rots or rusts his opponent's weapon to dust as it strikes his block. The Abyssal character's player rolls Dexterity + Melee in response to any close-range attack. If even one success is achieved, the attacker's weapon shatters to mildewed splinters and rust without injuring the defender. Should the target spend motes equal to the weapon's damage bonus plus one, so it costs 3 motes to disintegrate a short sword, 8 for a great axe, the character can only disintegrate actual weapons -- so no rotting off an aggressor's fist or claws. Also, this Charm cannot damage weapons made of Essence or the Five Magical Materials.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Melee tree ('Melee 3'), p. 171 (PDF 172). Flagged for re-verification: the mote-cost sentence structure ('Should the target spend motes...') reads awkwardly in this render and may describe the Abyssal, not the target, spending motes to trigger the disintegration; re-check against a cleaner render before promotion.

name: Attunement-Shattering Block
summary: Capstone of the third Dusk Caste Melee tree; the Abyssal can dispel the Essence empowering a magical weapon she parries, rendering it temporarily useless.
requirements: Minimum Melee 4; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Corrosive Parry.
mechanics: With this Charm, an Abyssal can dispel the Essence empowering a magical weapon, rendering it temporarily useless. This Charm may be activated whenever the deathknight parries a magical weapon; her player need not roll to deflect the attack entirely, but the Abyssal character's player must roll at least one success on the block attempt. This Charm costs 3 motes and 1 temporary Willpower. The defending character's player then makes a reflexive Essence + Melee roll, with a difficulty tied to the target's permanent Essence. If it succeeds, the weapon becomes an inert hunk of steel and Magical Materials, although it may be reattuned normally by its owner. Of course, this reattunement takes 15 or 30 minutes. The victim can avert deattunement by immediately spending a number of motes equal to the attunement cost of the weapon.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Melee tree ('Melee 3'), p. 171 (PDF 172).

name: Fluttering Moth Defense
summary: With growing mastery, the Abyssal's weapon dances to intercept attacks as a moth spiraling to a torch, adding her full Dexterity + Melee dice pool to parry a single close-range attack she is aware of.
requirements: Minimum Melee 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Elegant Flowing Deflection.
mechanics: With growing mastery, the Abyssal's weapon dances to intercept attacks as a moth spiraling to a torch. The deathknight's player may roll her character's full Dexterity + Melee dice pool to parry one close-range attack of which the Abyssal is aware.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Melee tree ('Melee 3'), pp. 171-172 (PDF 172-173); effect text continues onto the following page.

name: Hundred Razor Circle
summary: The best defense is a good offense: the Abyssal stands motionless and traces a lightning-fast pattern of strikes and slices around herself, automatically attacking anyone who approaches within three yards.
requirements: Minimum Melee 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Fluttering Moth Defense.
mechanics: Sometimes, the best defense is a good offense. Building on this principle, the Abyssal stands motionless and traces a lightning-fast pattern of slices and slices around herself. Anyone entering this warded circle risks terrible injury. The Exalt cannot actively attack, dodge or move faster than one yard per turn without breaking the Charm, but her player automatically rolls a full Dexterity + Melee attack against everyone who is currently within or who subsequently approaches within three yards of the character. The character may also reflexively attack incoming projectiles of which he is aware. This is a difficulty 4 Dexterity + Melee roll and adds the weapon's Parry modifier to the offending missile. Note that this Charm does not distinguish between friend or foe -- the Exalt must attack everyone in range.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Melee tree ('Melee 3'), p. 172 (PDF 173).

name: Incomparable Sentinel Stance
summary: The Abyssal may effortlessly deflect any attack she is aware of on a single reflexive roll, turning aside even normally-unparryable assaults like caustic slime or falling boulders.
requirements: Minimum Melee 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Hundred Razor Circle.
mechanics: The Abyssal may effortlessly deflect any attack she is aware of with a single reflexive roll. This Charm can turn aside assaults normally impossible to parry, such as gouts of caustic slime or the falling boulders of a landslide. The character can even parry the attacks of greater spirits and demon lords, although such onslaughts invariably shatter any non-magical weapon in the process. This is a perfect defense.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Melee tree ('Melee 3'), p. 172 (PDF 173).

name: Eye of the Tempest
summary: Capstone of the third Dusk Caste Melee tree; the Abyssal becomes a point of serene calm in a vortex of steel and howling shadows, parrying every physical attack she is aware of for a full scene.
requirements: Minimum Melee 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Hundred Razor Circle.
mechanics: With this Charm, the Abyssal becomes a point of serene calm in a vortex of steel and howling shadows. The deathknight's player may use his character's full Dexterity + Melee dice pool to parry all physical attacks of which the Abyssal is aware.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Melee tree ('Melee 3'), p. 172 (PDF 173). Closes out the Dusk Caste Melee section, the largest of the five Dusk Caste Ability trees (24 Charms across three sub-trees: Melee 1/2/3).

name: Hungry Missile Technique
summary: Root of the Dusk Caste Thrown tree; suffused with malevolent hunger, a thrown weapon leaps from the Abyssal's hand and turns in flight to pursue its prey, letting her spend Essence to weaken a defender's dice pool.
requirements: Minimum Thrown 2; Minimum Essence 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: Suffused with malevolent hunger, the character's weapon leaps from her hand and turns in flight to pursue its prey. After the target declares any defense, the Abyssal may activate this Charm to subtract one die per mote spent from the target's player's dice pool for a single Thrown attack the Abyssal makes. The Abyssal cannot spend more motes powering this Charm than required to reduce a victim's dice pool to his permanent Essence rating. If the target has Charms or other effects that allow multiple forms of defense, Hungry Missile Technique applies only to the first defense.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Thrown tree, p. 172 (PDF 173). Opens the Thrown section, the last of the five Dusk Caste Ability trees.

name: Lightning Clutch of the Raptor
summary: A character with this Charm moves with impossible speed to pluck arrows and other missile weapons from the air before they can hit her, reflexively parrying any ranged attack with her full dice pool.
requirements: Minimum Thrown 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Hungry Missile Technique.
mechanics: A character with this Charm moves with impossible speed to pluck arrows and other missile weapons from the air before they can hit her. The Abyssal may reflexively parry any ranged attack she is aware of with her full Dexterity + Thrown. If this roll leaves the attacker with no successes, the Exalt has successfully caught the projectile and may subsequently do with it whatever she wishes. Even if the defender fails to score more successes than her attacker, she still reduces the damage of the attack as normal, so the Charm is not an all-or-nothing proposition. The speed at which the character grabs incoming missiles is sufficient to douse most fires, including flames set by the Solar Charm Fiery Arrow Attack. The character cannot parry bolts of Essence or other purely mystical projectiles unless she has a permanent Essence of 3 or higher. If an Abyssal parries an intangible missile, it disperses harmlessly against her palm. Lightning Clutch of the Raptor may also be used to defend against ranged area-of-effect attacks such as the Death of Obsidian Butterflies; this costs 4 motes instead of 1, and the character only deflects missiles threatening her. Otherwise, parrying an area assault follows the same rules as any other application of this Charm.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Thrown tree, p. 172 (PDF 173). References Solar Charm Fiery Arrow Attack and the Death of Obsidian Butterflies (a necromancy spell not yet inventoried here) as external comparisons.

name: Incomparable Assassin Method
summary: An Abyssal with this Charm instinctively knows where and how to throw a weapon to deliver a fatal blow, guaranteeing lethal damage and doubling damage on a killing strike.
requirements: Minimum Thrown 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Hungry Missile Technique.
mechanics: An Abyssal with this Charm instinctively knows where and how to throw her weapon to deliver a fatal blow. The player makes an attack roll as normal, but the damage is doubled after it is rolled. However, if this is not enough to kill the target outright, the strike only inflicts one automatic unsoakable health level of damage. As an ancillary benefit, the character's attack inflicts lethal damage (at least 1L) if it didn't already, so this attack can be used to throw tiny or unconventional weapons such as dominos with Range 10, Accuracy +0, Rate 3.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Thrown tree, p. 172 (PDF 173).

name: Aid of Ill Wind
summary: Second root of the Dusk Caste Thrown tree; the Abyssal lightens her weapon as she launches it, buoying its flight with a spectral gust from the Underworld to multiply its range.
requirements: Minimum Thrown 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: The Abyssal lightens her weapon as she launches it, buoying its flight with a spectral gust from the Underworld. The weapon's range increases by one factor for every 2 motes spent. Thus, a character that spends 2 motes doubles her attack's range, while one who spends 4 motes triples it, etc. Characters cannot spend more than 2-mote increments activating this Charm than they have points of permanent Essence.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Thrown tree, p. 173 (PDF 174).

name: Ivory Spine Attack
summary: The Abyssal extrudes a slender bone needle from her palm or fingertip, fires it with a subtle flick of the wrist, and can channel Essence through her entire skeleton to saturate an area with hundreds of paralytic needles.
requirements: Minimum Thrown 4; Minimum Medicine 1; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Aid of Ill Wind.
mechanics: With a subtle flick of her wrist, an Abyssal who knows this Charm may extrude a slender bone needle from her palm or finger -- no more than the length of a child's finger -- but its paralytic venom coating helps make up for its tiny size. Needles created with this Charm have a base lethal Accuracy and Range in yards equal to five times its base value. Note that other magic, although attack successes contribute normally. Needles do not add Strength for determining damage, although attack successes contribute normally. Needles remain envenomed for one hour after creation. Players of unarmored characters struck by a poisoned needle must reflexively roll Stamina + Resistance against a difficulty of the Abyssal's Medicine score. Exalted victims who fail this roll suffer levels of unsoakable lethal damage equal to the deathknight's Essence. UnExalted victims whose players fail die instantly unless one day treated with curative magic. The Abyssal Exalt is naturally immune to her own poison.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Thrown tree, p. 173 (PDF 174). Flagged for re-verification: this render's effect paragraph repeats the 'attack successes contribute normally' clause twice and the Range multiplier/Medicine-difficulty sentence structure reads ambiguously; re-check against a cleaner render before promotion. Unusual in requiring a minimum rating in a second Ability (Medicine 1) alongside Thrown.

name: Burrowing Bone Maggot
summary: The Abyssal flings a sliver of gleaming bone that burrows into a living victim's body and continues its slow, painful journey toward the heart until surgically removed.
requirements: Minimum Thrown 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Ivory Spine Attack.
mechanics: With this Charm, an Abyssal may fling a splinter of gleaming bone at his target. Upon striking a living victim, the spine rapidly burrows into her body and begins its painful journey toward her heart. The needle has the same statistics as one created with Ivory Spine Attack, although it is not poisonous. Rather, if it successfully hits a victim, it begins inflicting one dice of unsoakable lethal damage each minute. This damage continues until the Abyssal wills the needle to temporarily stop. The Abyssal can later will the needle to resume its path at any time. The spine itself will remain in existence as long as the Abyssal leaves Good intent committed to it or until its victim dies. Skilled doctors can sometimes remove a Burrowing Bone Maggot, but the surgery has a minimum difficulty of 4 and requires a sharp knife and the surgeon's undivided dice action for 10 turns (half a minute).
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Thrown tree, p. 173 (PDF 174). Flagged for re-verification: the sentence describing how long the spine persists ('as long as the Abyssal leaves Good intent committed to it') reads as a probable OCR/visual misread of a different phrase (likely 'as long as the Abyssal leaves the needle committed to it' or similar); re-check against a cleaner render before promotion.

name: Thousand Needle Torrent
summary: The Abyssal channels Essence through her entire skeleton, growing hundreds of Essence-laden bone needles that erupt in seconds and saturate a wide radius with lethal, razor-sharp spikes.
requirements: Minimum Thrown 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Ivory Spine Attack.
mechanics: The character channels Essence through her entire skeleton, growing hundreds of Essence-laden bone needles similar to those produced with Ivory Spine Attack. Within seconds, the needles tear through her skin at high velocity, saturating the immediate area with razor-sharp spikes. Everyone within five yards of the Exalt suffers lethal damage (Stamina + Thrown + Essence) equal to the Abyssal's Stamina + Thrown + Essence. This damage is reduced by one die for every yard further out, so victims six yards away suffer (Stamina + Thrown + Essence - 1)L, etc. This damage cannot be dodged or blocked without a stunt or Charm. Successes on dodge or block attempts reduce the damage by 1L per success. Needles created with this Charm disintegrate seconds after their explosive flight. Armored characters may not use this Charm, as their armor blunts the explosion.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Thrown tree, p. 173 (PDF 174).

name: Pitiless Scything Razor
summary: A thrown weapon enchanted with this Charm becomes an extension of its owner's malice, ricocheting between every target in range like a swooping bird of prey.
requirements: Minimum Thrown 5; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Incomparable Assassin Method, Aid of Ill Wind.
mechanics: A thrown weapon enchanted with this Charm becomes an extension of its owner's malice, arcing and ricocheting from one target to the next like a swooping bird of prey. The weapon makes a number of separate attacks equal to the character's Thrown score, with no subtractions for multiple actions. If an attack misses, the weapon simply moves on to its next target. However, if any roll botches, the weapon strikes an unintended victim and falls to the ground. Otherwise, the weapon faithfully returns to its master's hand at the end of the turn. All targets of Pitiless Scything Razor must be in range when the character first throws the weapon, and no target may be hit more than once by a given weapon during a single use of this Charm.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Thrown tree, pp. 173-174 (PDF 174-175); effect text continues onto the following page.

name: Ravening Crimson Chakram
summary: Capstone of the Dusk Caste Thrown tree; a weapon imbued with a measure of its master's bloodlust leaps from the Abyssal's hand to slake the life energy of its prey, feeding on every target it strikes across multiple attacks.
requirements: Minimum Thrown 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Pitiless Scything Razor.
mechanics: Imbued with a measure of its master's bloodlust, a weapon enchanted with this Charm leaps from its master's hand to slake the life energy of its prey. Ravening Crimson Chakram duplicates the effects of Pitiless Scything Razor with two key differences: first, the thrown weapon can attack the same target more than once. Second, the weapon actually feeds on its Essence for every health level of damage inflicted after soak. If the Abyssal's player does not botch any attack rolls, the deathknight gains all harvested motes when he recovers his weapon at the end of the turn. Soulsteel throwing weapons also drain motes as normal for each attack.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Dusk Caste Thrown tree, p. 174 (PDF 175). Closes out the entire Dusk Caste Charm set (Archery, Brawl, Martial Arts, Melee, Thrown -- 65 Charms total).

name: Ox-Body Technique (Abyssal)
summary: Opens the Midnight Caste Endurance tree; lets an Abyssal buy extra health levels as if they were a Charm, purchasable once per dot of Endurance, matching the Charm's standard cross-splat form.
requirements: Minimum Endurance: Varies; Minimum Essence 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: As befitting the champions of the Underworld, Abyssal Exalted are far more resilient than mere mortals and may purchase extra health levels as if it were a Charm. This Charm can be taken as many times as a character has dots of Endurance. Each Ox-Body Technique purchased provides one of the following, decided by the player at the time of purchase: one -0 health level; two -1 health levels; or one -1 health level and two -2 health levels.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Endurance tree, p. 174 (PDF 175). Named identically to the Lunar/Solar Ox-Body Technique (see the Lunar family's `ox-body-technique` row) but is a distinct per-family Charm entry keyed to Endurance rather than Stamina; given a disambiguated id (`ox-body-technique-abyssal`) to avoid a cross-family id collision even though ids are only required to be unique within this family.

name: Ghost Armor Prana
summary: Root of the first Midnight Caste Endurance tree; the Abyssal enfolds her anima about her armor, granting it surreal lightness and reducing its fatigue and mobility burdens.
requirements: Minimum Endurance 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: The Abyssal enfolds her anima about her armor, granting it surreal lightness for an hour. For every 3 motes spent, the character reduces the fatigue value and mobility penalty of her armor by one point, to a maximum possible reduction equal to her permanent Essence. A fatigue value of zero indicates the character need never roll to see if she becomes fatigued from wearing her armor. This Charm cannot reduce a character's mobility penalty or fatigue value below zero.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Endurance tree ('Endurance 1'), p. 174 (PDF 175).

name: Tireless Sentinel Technique
summary: An Abyssal with this Charm can reinvigorate herself with Essence, acting or standing watch without penalty for sleep loss or exhaustion far longer than natural rest allows, at the price of eventual bashing damage.
requirements: Minimum Endurance 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Ghost Armor Prana.
mechanics: An Abyssal with this Charm can reinvigorate herself with Essence, allowing him to act or stand watch without penalties for sleep loss or exhaustion. There is no limit to how many days this Charm can be used in a row, but maintaining Essence is a poor substitute for natural rest. After a number of days equal to the character's Stamina + Endurance, the Exalt begins to suffer one unsoakable level of bashing damage each time the Charm is used. This damage does not heal until the character stops using the Charm. Once a character ends use of Tireless Sentinel Technique, he cannot safely reactivate it until all damage from the Charm has been healed. Doing otherwise only continues the process of decay.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Endurance tree ('Endurance 1'), p. 175 (PDF 176).

name: Relentless Revenant Spirit
summary: Capstone of the first Midnight Caste Endurance tree; once an Abyssal learns it, death itself cannot stop him, rising as an unusually capable, self-willed ghost if slain.
requirements: Minimum Endurance 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Tireless Sentinel Technique.
mechanics: Once an Abyssal learns this Charm, death itself cannot stop him. If slain, his spirit rises again as a ghost. He loses his Exaltation and its commensurate power, but he gains the full advantages of unlife, retains the ability to use any supernatural martial-arts forms he may know up to and including the Form (but not more advanced techniques), and gains twice as many Arcanoi as a starting ghost. The Storyteller has final say on what Traits the character keeps and how many ghost Charms he can purchase, etc.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Endurance tree ('Endurance 1'), p. 175 (PDF 176). Positioned in the tree diagram as a sibling of Tireless Sentinel Technique under Ghost Armor Prana, but the body text's Prerequisite Charms line names Tireless Sentinel Technique specifically; treated the body text as authoritative over the diagram's apparent branching.

name: Pain-Eating Focus
summary: Root of the second Midnight Caste Endurance tree; the Abyssal understands the power of suffering and hate, letting her harvest Essence from her own wounds in combat.
requirements: Minimum Endurance 1; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: More than any of the other Chosen, the Abyssal Exalted understand the power of suffering and hate. A character with this Charm may invoke it whenever she is struck in combat. For every die of pre-soak damage the attack inflicts, her player may roll one die. Each success on this roll restores 1 mote of Essence, up to the character's usual limit. A character cannot harvest more Essence from a single attack than her Essence rating.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Endurance tree ('Endurance 2'), p. 175 (PDF 176).

name: Insensible Corpse Technique
summary: Capstone of the second Midnight Caste Endurance tree; many Abyssals learn to dampen pain with Essence, either permanently inuring themselves against wound penalties or spending motes for temporary numbing.
requirements: Minimum Endurance 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Pain-Eating Focus.
mechanics: Many Abyssal Exalted show disturbing indifference to suffering. When this Charm is purchased, the player must decide whether to permanently inure the Exalt against the worst of his pain or cultivate a more powerful numbing for short-term use. In the former case, the Exalt permanently subtracts 2 from all wound penalties. Such anesthetizing does not accelerate healing, so a -2 level reduced to -0 still regenerates as a -2. However, this penalty reduction is cumulative, so characters buying this Charm twice subtract 4 from their wound penalties. Once this Charm is purchased three times, the Exalt is thereafter immune to all but the most unimaginably terrible agony. In its configuration as a temporary anesthetic, this Charm allows characters to dampen pain with Essence. For every mote spent, the Exalt can ignore one die of wound penalties. This Charm can be used multiple times in a scene, with cumulative effect. Characters can even negate more dice of wound penalties than they suffer from wound penalties for future injury. Exalted who know the temporary and permanent form of this Charm combine both effects when determining their final wound penalty reduction.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Endurance tree ('Endurance 2'), pp. 175-176 (PDF 176-177); effect text continues onto the following page.

name: Agony-Savoring Spirit
summary: Where an Abyssal with Pain-Eating Focus draws power from her own torment, a character with this Charm can instead feed on the suffering of others whenever she personally slays a victim.
requirements: Minimum Endurance 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Pain-Eating Focus.
mechanics: Where an Abyssal with Pain-Eating Focus draws power from her own torment, a character with this Charm can feed on the suffering of others. A character can use this Charm whenever she slays an individual single-handedly. The Abyssal's player rolls Conviction. Each success restores one point of Willpower.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Endurance tree ('Endurance 2'), p. 176 (PDF 177). Closes out the Midnight Caste Endurance section (7 Charms total including Ox-Body Technique).

name: Haunting Inflection Trick
summary: Root of the Midnight Caste Performance tree; as the Exalt speaks, her voice takes on an otherworldly tone, letting her add extra dice to Performance or Presence rolls that use her voice.
requirements: Minimum Performance 2; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: As the Exalt speaks, her voice takes on an otherworldly tone. Whether shattered into multiple discordant pitches or augmented to mellifluous grace, her augmented tone adds emotional weight to everything she says. The character can add 2 dice to a Performance or Presence dice pool for every mote spent, although she may not more than double her pool. The character must be employing her voice to invoke this Charm, whether for singing, teaching or oration.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Performance tree, p. 176 (PDF 177). Tree diagram on this page shows two roots (Morbid Fascination Style and Haunting Inflection Trick) feeding a shared web of six further Charms.

name: Withering Dirge
summary: A deathknight channels Essence into a mournful song so that members of her audience, willing or otherwise, start to die as they listen, their life Essence sucked away into the Underworld.
requirements: Minimum Performance 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Haunting Inflection Trick.
mechanics: A deathknight can channel Essence into a mournful song so that members of his audience, willing or otherwise, start to die as they listen to it. Their bodies weaken as their life Essence is sucked away into the Underworld. Each listener suffers 1L for every 2 motes spent on the Charm, up to a maximum damage equal to the deathknight's permanent Essence. This damage leaves no physical mark and may only be soaked with Stamina or soak-boosting Charms. Characters can only activate this Charm once per turn, although they may activate it on subsequent turns to continue their song unabated. The exact nature of a Withering Dirge depends on the Abyssal, but there is no mechanical difference between an achingly beautiful requiem and a piercing scream of anguish. Nonliving beings and the deaf are immune to this Charm.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Performance tree, p. 176 (PDF 177).

name: Elegy for the Fallen
summary: Preaching the veneration of death and the dead, a memorial ritual an Abyssal channels through a living congregation or an assembled crowd of the honored dead to empower the Underworld.
requirements: Minimum Performance 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Haunting Inflection Trick.
mechanics: Preaching the veneration of death and the dead knights, such adulation serves to strengthen the power of the Underworld and garnering useful allies among the dead. To these ends, Abyssal Exalted with this Charm may channel the prayers of a living congregation to empower the dead, or channel a memorial service directed at a single ghost or the dead in general, as decided by the Exalt, but such worship can only be carried out at night. If targeting a single ghost, the Abyssal spends one or more hours leading his assembled congregation in prayers to the honored deceased. Such prayers can take the form of a high ritual, a mournful song or dance -- even a lighthearted wake. After each hour, the character's player rolls dice equal to the number of active participants. The total number of dice count as greater than twice the deathknight's Charisma + Performance. A ghost who is subject of such a celebration regains 1 mote of Essence for every success rolled -- or half that number if he is not physically present at the memorial. If used to facilitate general worship of death, this Charm uses the same system. However, the total Essence generated is divided evenly among all ghosts through the mausoleums of Stygia.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Performance tree, p. 177 (PDF 178). Flagged for re-verification: the sentence 'The total number of dice count as greater than twice the deathknight's Charisma + Performance' reads ambiguously in this render (likely means the dice pool is capped at twice Charisma + Performance rather than literally 'greater than'); re-check against a cleaner render before promotion.

name: Lamenting Ghost Technique
summary: Transforms the Abyssal's voice into a terrible weapon, screaming a devastating sonic blast that harms a single target from far beyond ordinary vocal range.
requirements: Minimum Performance 5; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Withering Dirge.
mechanics: An Abyssal with this Charm can transform her voice into a terrible weapon. The character opens her mouth wide and screams, pouring Essence into a devastating sonic blast. The character's player rolls Manipulation + Performance to hit a single target, inflicting a base damage of 1L for every mote of Essence spent. Extra successes add as normal. This attack cannot be parried, only dodged, and can be soaked only with Stamina and other natural soak enhancers. Lamenting Ghost Technique has a range of (the character's Performance x 10) yards. An Abyssal may not spend more motes powering this Charm than her Stamina + Essence.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Performance tree, p. 177 (PDF 178).

name: Morbid Fascination Style
summary: Second root of the Midnight Caste Performance tree; with a thought, the Abyssal can instantly command fear and respect from an assembled crowd, curdling any dislike into grudging deference.
requirements: Minimum Performance 2; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: With this Charm, an Abyssal may instantly command fear and respect from an assembled crowd. Audience members may not like her performance or believe her words, but they recognize the implicit malice she embodies and treat her accordingly. In short, they may not like her, but they know better than to heckle or depart before the end of the show. A few disturbed souls may actually find the Abyssal more alluring as a result of her dangerous edge, but these are the exception, not the rule. This Charm only works on non-magical beings.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Performance tree, p. 177 (PDF 178).

name: Heart-Sculpting Oration
summary: An Abyssal with this Charm can inflame or harden the passions of the living and the dead alike, selecting an emotion and forcing a crowd toward it unless their Willpower resists.
requirements: Minimum Performance 5; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Haunting Inflection Trick, Morbid Fascination Style.
mechanics: An Abyssal with this Charm can inflame or harden the passions of the living and the dead alike. The character speaks with smoldering fervor or cold certainty, lending supernatural conviction to her words and mannerisms. Her player selects an emotion and rolls Manipulation + Performance at difficulty 2. If the desired emotion is innately negative -- such as hate, fear or sorrow -- this roll is made at standard difficulty. Targets whose Willpower score is less than the number of successes rolled are completely overwhelmed by the emotional onslaught and act accordingly. A crowd suffused with rage as right as riot, while a criminal monk overcome with lust seeks to indulge his previously repressed desire. Targets with a Willpower less than twice the number of successes rolled may make a Willpower roll (difficulty 1) to resist the emotion. Individuals whose Willpower exceeds twice the successes rolled are completely unaffected. The emotional tampering caused by this Charm only lasts for one scene, although low-Temperance characters may continue to indulge themselves for some time afterward, at Storyteller discretion. This Charm can also induce apathy, rather than passion. This requires the same roll, but affected targets find themselves emotionally numbed. Everything feels crushingly bleak and hollow. This effect can be used to quell riots, as apathetic mobs quickly lose inertia and disperse.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Performance tree, p. 177 (PDF 178). Flagged for re-verification: the sentence 'A crowd suffused with rage as right as riot' reads as a probable transcription artifact of a different original phrase (likely something like 'A crowd suffused with rage rises up in riot'); re-check against a cleaner render before promotion.

name: Morale-Shattering Method
summary: An Abyssal who knows this Charm can radiate a nimbus of cold dread that saps the morale of enemies within a wide radius, penalizing their combat dice pools and Valor rolls for a scene.
requirements: Minimum Performance 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Withering Dirge, Heart-Sculpting Oration.
mechanics: An Abyssal Exalt who knows this Charm can radiate a nimbus of cold dread that saps the morale of enemies. All enemy troops within a radius of (the character's Conviction x 100) yards ensorcelled with this Charm lose 1 die from all combat dice pools and their players suffer a +1 difficulty on all Valor rolls. The effect of this Charm on the overall outcome of a battle rests within the Storyteller's discretion, but its influence should be considerable.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Performance tree, p. 178 (PDF 179).

name: Hardened Killer Training Style
summary: Capstone of the Midnight Caste Performance tree; a brutal training regimen that transforms motley crews of peaceful mortals and children into competent, psychotically merciless killers within weeks.
requirements: Minimum Performance 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Morale-Shattering Method.
mechanics: Although many deathknight generals prefer mute legions of zombies to unpredictable mortal troops, a few recognize the power of the human spirit in crushing that spirit to serve the will of the Deathlords. Abyssals who know this Charm can transform a motley crew of peaceful mortals and children into competent merciless killers with disturbing ease. Characters may supervise a maximum of (their Essence rating x 100) soldiers in a given week. Soldiers trained for a month or longer are considered elite troops. They are quite disciplined, with relevant combat Abilities rated at 3 or higher and usually a specialty or two in a favored weapon. More importantly, this brutal training regimen gradually wears away humanity and replaces it with psychotic malice. For every two weeks that a soldier undergoes this instruction, she loses one dot of Compassion and gains a dot of either Valor or Conviction. By the time they graduate, the new soldiers typically have Compassion 1 and five or more dots divided between Conviction and Valor. Continued use of this Charm only further increases the combat prowess of the Abyssal's troops.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Performance tree, p. 178 (PDF 179). Closes out the Midnight Caste Performance section (8 Charms total).

name: Elegant Tyrant's Majesty
summary: Root of the Midnight Caste Presence tree; an Abyssal using this Charm radiates terrible allure, adding dice to Presence, Socialize and Bureaucracy rolls and letting her bark commands that ordinary victims cannot resist.
requirements: Minimum Presence 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: An Abyssal using this Charm radiates terrible allure. His words resound with unholy power and conviction, while his every gesture bespeaks grace and nobility. The Exalt's player adds a number of dice equal to his character's Essence to all Presence, Socialize and Bureaucracy rolls involving one-on-one interaction. This bonus also applies to all intimidation attempts, regardless of the number of onlookers present. Note that this Charm engenders respect and fear -- it does not win friends or make the Exalt more likeable. The Exalt's player rolls Manipulation + Presence against a difficulty of the target's permanent Essence. If targeting multiple beings, use the highest Essence rating in the group. The amount of control the character has depends on the number of successes rolled. One success is sufficient to bark simple harmless commands that do not violate the target's Nature ('Back off!' for example). With three successes, the target must completely obey the Exalt, although sentient targets may ignore commands that would cause them physical harm. With five successes, the target does anything the Exalt commands for the duration of the Charm. Keep in mind that the walking dead aren't the brightest creatures and have difficulty comprehending anything more complicated than a simple sentence. While more intelligent, ghosts are similarly limited by language. The Exalt cannot obey instructions they do not understand, regardless of their degree of obedience. Ensorcelled targets never attack their master, however -- at least, not until they regain their own free will. An Abyssal may also use Command the Dead to usurp control of walking dead and ghosts from other necromancers. This follows the same rules, except that the difficulty is the Essence rating of the targets' current master. Characters cannot usurp control from necromancers with a higher permanent Essence than their own.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Presence tree, p. 179 (PDF 180). The Command the Dead usurpation paragraph appears embedded in this Charm's own text block but describes Command the Dead's function; likely a page-layout artifact of the two-column render rather than part of Elegant Tyrant's Majesty proper -- flagged for re-verification of exact paragraph ownership before promotion.

name: Command the Dead
summary: An Abyssal using this Charm may issue orders to the dead and demand their obedience, controlling mindless undead cheaply and true ghosts at steeper cost provided her Essence exceeds theirs.
requirements: Minimum Presence 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Elegant Tyrant's Majesty.
mechanics: An Abyssal using this Charm may issue orders to the dead and demand their obedience. If targeting mindless undead or hungry ghosts, the cost of the Charm is 5 motes, plus 1 mote for every additional target beyond the first. Actual ghosts require 10 motes, plus 3 motes per additional target, and the Exalt must have a permanent Essence of 3 or higher to control such beings.
cost: 5/10 motes, 1 Willpower + 1/3 motes per additional target
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Presence tree, p. 179 (PDF 180).

name: Skeleton Summoning Gesture
summary: Capstone of one Presence sub-branch; the Abyssal channels a burst of Essence into the ground, raising an army of common zombie skeletons largely from a graveyard's worth of buried dead.
requirements: Minimum Presence 3; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Command the Dead.
mechanics: The Abyssal channels a burst of Essence into the ground beneath her feet. If a largely whole skeleton is in the vicinity, it claws its way out of the ground and emerges at the beginning of the next turn. Skeletons raised with this Charm are their maker to the best of their limited intelligence and have the same statistics as common zombies. These monsters are always extras.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Presence tree, pp. 179-180 (PDF 180-181); cost/header on p. 179, effect text continues on p. 180 (PDF 181). Cross-references core Exalted p. 298 for common zombie statistics. Flagged for re-verification: 'raised with this Charm are their maker to the best of their limited intelligence' reads as a probable transcription artifact for 'obey their maker to the best of their limited intelligence.'

name: Irresistible Succubus Style
summary: Heightens an Abyssal's cold beauty, transforming her visage to match her idealized form and adding her Essence to her Appearance while cloaked in an illusion that ordinary Temperance-checking victims find nearly impossible to resist.
requirements: Minimum Presence 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Elegant Tyrant's Majesty.
mechanics: Irresistible Succubus Style heightens an Abyssal's cold beauty, transforming her visage to match her idealized form. Deathknights using this Charm are alabaster angels or onyx goddesses, achingly beautiful apparitions with flawless skin and ruby lips. A character adds her permanent Essence to her Appearance rating as long as she remains enchanted. This metamorphosis is illusion, however, but ideal to their life with Essence. As such, the character's altered beauty cannot be pierced by magic that detects glamour or illusion. In addition to augmenting her beauty, this Charm also causes the Abyssal to exude an aura of seduction. Players of characters who behold the Exalt or interact with her must make a successful Temperance roll. If the roll fails, the characters find the Abyssal overwhelmingly desirable regardless of their normal sexual preference. They will not harm the Exalt and are likely to behave irrationally in an attempt to impress her. If the Exalt actually wishes to seduce a smitten character, she may do so without a roll. This aura has no effect on beings with an Essence rating higher than the Exalt invoking the Charm, nor does it affect the Fair Folk. Similarly, this aura has no effect on beings engaged in combat or otherwise believe the Abyssal means them harm. Overtly hostile acts on the part of the Exalt may render a particular subject immune but do not prevent this Charm from enthralling others.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Presence tree, p. 180 (PDF 181).

name: Soul-Flaying Gaze
summary: By staring intently at a target, an Abyssal with this Charm can sap that victim's will and subjugate her spirit, entrancing the loser of a resisted Manipulation + Presence contest into obeying her every whim.
requirements: Minimum Presence 4; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Elegant Tyrant's Majesty.
mechanics: By staring intently at a target, an Abyssal with this Charm can sap that victim's will and subjugate her spirit. The target must be within five yards and must be able to see the Exalt when Soul-Flaying Gaze is invoked. If these conditions are met, the target finds her vision drawn to the deathknight's own eyes. As their gazes connect, the Abyssal's player rolls Manipulation + Presence in a resisted roll against the target's Willpower. If the Exalt wins, the target is immediately entranced and can take no further actions that turn. Additionally, the victim loses a number of points of Willpower equal to the Abyssal's permanent Essence. If the target wins, the Charm has no effect. A character who loses all Willpower from this Charm becomes highly suggestible to the Abyssal. Although she cannot be ordered to do anything to harm herself or others (unless naturally predisposed to do so), such a hapless individual otherwise obeys the Exalt for the rest of the scene. This control shatters immediately if the victim suffers actual damage, and she may regain lost Willpower normally.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Presence tree, p. 180 (PDF 181).

name: Compelling Whisper Technique
summary: Layering her speech with a haunting chorus of voices, the Abyssal can implant hidden commands in a target's psyche, sustaining a covert delayed-trigger suggestion for days at a time.
requirements: Minimum Presence 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Soul-Flaying Gaze.
mechanics: Layering her speech with a haunting chorus of voices, the Abyssal can implant hidden commands in a target's psyche. Roll the character's Manipulation + Presence in a resisted contest against the target's Willpower. If the target wins, she immediately knows what the Exalt attempted to do and the precise conditions of the suggestion. If the Exalt wins, however, he may issue one order. This instruction can be as simple or complicated as desired, but the intended task cannot take longer than the Exalt's Essence in turns. The suggestion remains until its conditions are met or a number of days equal to the Manipulation of the Exalt have passed. During this time, the target has no conscious recollection of her orders. Even after the target carries out her instructions, she does not recall the act unless specified to do so. Even if she remembers her actions, she does not connect them with a hypnotic suggestion unless she has other reason to believe such tampering occurred. This Charm cannot make characters hurt themselves or others unless they are already strongly predisposed to do so.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Presence tree, p. 181 (PDF 182).

name: Heart-Stopping Mien
summary: Capstone of the Midnight Caste Presence tree; the Abyssal blazes with unimaginable soul-chilling horror, punishing anyone who dares attack or approach her with unsoakable lethal damage or debilitating fear.
requirements: Minimum Presence 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Soul-Flaying Gaze.
mechanics: An Abyssal with this Charm blazes with unholy power and radiates unimaginable soul-chilling horror, causing his anima to flare as if he had spent 15 motes of Peripheral Essence. While Heart-Stopping Mien is in effect, a successful reflexive Valor roll is required each turn to attack the character or to voluntarily approach within two yards of him. If an aggressor fails, she suffers unsoakable lethal damage equal to the Abyssal's Essence rating. Characters that suffer more damage in this fashion on a turn than their Stamina spend the rest of the turn writhing in agony and lose their action. Injuries inflicted by this Charm typically manifest as heart attacks or strokes, although more exotic torments are not unheard of. Magical beings (including other Exalted) do not suffer this damage but, instead, cannot attack the deathknight on a turn that their players fail a Valor roll. Those who attack the Abyssal do so at a die penalty equal to the deathknight's permanent Essence. This Charm is not compatible with the Dusk Caste anima power.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Presence tree, cost block on p. 181 (PDF 182), effect text continues onto p. 182 (PDF 183). Closes out the Midnight Caste Presence section (7 Charms total).

name: Spirit-Hardened Frame
summary: Root of the Midnight Caste Resistance tree; the Exalted channels calcifying death Essence through his body, granting his flesh the resilience of leathery, wind-dried tissue.
requirements: Minimum Resistance 2; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: The Exalted channels calcifying death Essence through his body, granting his flesh the resilience of leathery, wind-dried tissue. For every 2 motes of Essence spent, the character may add one point to his bashing soak. Additionally, the character can add half this bonus to his lethal soak (rounded down). Although this Charm can be activated multiple times in a scene to stack protection, the total bashing soak cannot exceed a character's Stamina + Resistance (or half that value for lethal soak). Spirit-Hardened Frame is compatible with armor.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Resistance tree ('Resistance 1'), p. 181 (PDF 182).

name: Ivory Blossom Carapace
