Characters cannot move in the same turn that they invoke Falling Scythe Attack, which precludes it from being placed in a Combo with Charms that involve or require movement, such as Flickering Image Strike. This Charm can be placed in a Combo with Spider Pounce Technique in order to extend the character's jumping attack, but this does not further increase the strike's damage. This Charm is explicitly permitted to be part of a Combo with Charms of other Abilities.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Athletics tree, p. 201 (PDF 202).

name: Soaring Raptor Prana
summary: Combines gliding descent with a diving strike, capping the Athletics 1 branch of the Day Caste tree.
requirements: Minimum Athletics 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Autumn Leaf's Descent, Falling Scythe Attack.
mechanics: The Charm header, cost, duration, type, and full prerequisites were confirmed directly from the printed Charm tree diagram and from cross-references in Autumn Leaf's Descent and Falling Scythe Attack, but the complete rules-text paragraph runs onto a portion of the page spread that was not legible in this extraction pass. Treat the full effect text as unresolved pending a follow-up close read of the surrounding page.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Athletics tree, p. 201-202 (PDF 202-203). Full rules text not fully legible in the rendered capture; flagged for a follow-up close read before promotion.

name: Shadow Races the Light
summary: This Charm increases speed for short bursts; the Exalt surges ahead in a muted blur of motion, her features obscured in trailing wisps of shadow, spending Essence each turn to multiply sprinting distance.
requirements: Minimum Athletics 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Raiton's Nimble Perch.
mechanics: With this Charm, a character may dramatically increase her speed for short bursts. Upon activation, the Exalt surges ahead in a muted blur of motion, her features obscured in trailing wisps of shadow. She may increase her sprinting speed by one factor for every 2 motes spent, up to a maximum multiplier of her permanent Essence. For example, a character with an Essence rating of 2 can spend 4 motes to triple her normal sprinting distance for the turn. As an additional benefit, characters employing this Charm can run without fear of winding or weariness.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Athletics tree, p. 202 (PDF 203).

name: Flickering Image Strike
summary: With this Charm, an Abyssal delivers a single devastating blow as she rushes past an opponent while sprinting, moving up to her normal sprinting distance and striking with doubled damage.
requirements: Minimum Athletics 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Shadow Races the Light.
mechanics: With this Charm, an Exalt delivers a single devastating blow as she rushes past an opponent. While executing this attack, the Abyssal is a flickering blur of violence and shadow -- her motions appear broken as if viewed by the light of a pulsing strobe. The character makes her attack normally, but the damage is doubled after it is rolled. The Exalt can move up to her normal sprinting distance without penalty on the same turn she activates this Charm, although she is not required to do so. She must have relative freedom of motion, however, so restrained characters cannot use this Charm. Flickering Image Strike is explicitly permitted to be part of Combos with Charms of other Abilities.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Athletics tree, p. 202 (PDF 203).

name: Crouching Gargoyle Stance
summary: The character hunches and stretches in unnatural angles, gaining unnatural flexibility and balance so she can scuttle or dash along any surface, cling to a ceiling, or perch at odd angles motionless.
requirements: Minimum Athletics 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Shadow Races the Light.
mechanics: The character hunches and stretches in unnatural angles, gaining unnatural flexibility and balance for as long as she maintains this Charm. The Exalt can scuttle or dash along any surface without regard to gravity, allowing him to scale sheer walls or dance on a ceiling with equal facility. Alternately, the character may stand motionless at odd angles or cling to an imperceptible perch. Storytellers should assign bonuses as appropriate. While useful, the character's distended limbs and joints reduce his Appearance by 1, to a minimum rating of zero. The Exalt must pay 1 mote each turn he maintains this Charm; this expenditure is reflexive and requires no concentration. If the character does not pay this upkeep, his body returns to normal configuration, and he once again becomes subject to gravity and inertia. All Essence spent on Crouching Gargoyle Stance remains committed until the Charm expires.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Athletics tree, p. 202 (PDF 203).

name: Mist Over Ice
summary: Stepping with the weightless poise of a ghost, the character can tread on water and other fluid surfaces as easily as solid ground, leaving no ripples, wake, or footprint sign.
requirements: Minimum Athletics 5; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Shadow Races the Light.
mechanics: Stepping with the weightless poise of a ghost, a character with this Charm can tread on water and other fluid surfaces as easily as solid ground. Her silent footfalls leave no ripples or wake, no sign to mark her passage as corporeal. Although the character can walk on dangerous liquids such as corrosive slime or magma without sinking, such landscapes still inflict normal injury to the soles of her feet or shoes. Characters must spend 2 motes each turn that they maintain Mist Over Ice. This upkeep is reflexive and does not require significant effort, but the overall concentration necessary to maintain this Charm adds +1 to the difficulty of all complex tasks (as decided by the Storyteller). If a character fails to pay this upkeep, all Essence spent on Mist Over Ice remains committed until the Exalt stops using this Charm.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Athletics tree, p. 203 (PDF 204).

name: Enhanced (Attribute) Discipline
summary: Suffusing his flesh and bones with Essence, the Abyssal briefly elevates his physical prowess; the character chooses to heighten either Strength or Dexterity, tracked as separate purchases (Enhanced Strength Discipline / Enhanced Dexterity Discipline).
requirements: Minimum Athletics 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: Suffusing his flesh and bones with Essence, the Abyssal briefly elevates his physical prowess to superhuman levels. When he purchases this Charm, the character must choose whether to heighten agility or power. This choice determines whether the character increases Strength or Dexterity. This Charm can be purchased again, so the character may eventually learn both the Strength and Dexterity versions. For every 3 motes spent, the character raises Strength by one dot. For every 5 motes spent, Dexterity increases by one dot. The character cannot increase an Attribute by more than his permanent Essence rating.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Athletics tree, pp. 203-204 (PDF 204-205). Purchased/tracked separately as Enhanced Strength Discipline or Enhanced Dexterity Discipline; the printed Athletics 3 sub-tree diagram shows the Strength branch feeding Infirmity Inflicting Gesture and Strength Stealing Technique.

name: Infirmity Inflicting Gesture
summary: With this Charm, an Abyssal can sap an enemy's vigor, draining a living target's Strength via a Willpower contest and leaving him weakened for the rest of the scene (or permanently if reduced to zero and non-magical).
requirements: Minimum Athletics 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Enhanced Strength Discipline (Enhanced (Attribute) Discipline, Strength focus).
mechanics: With this Charm, an Abyssal can sap an enemy's vigor and leave him enfeebled. The character gestures, and a wave of smothering Essence leaps from her fingers to any living target within five yards. The player makes a Willpower roll against a difficulty equal to the target's permanent Essence. If the roll is successful, the victim loses 1 dot of Strength for every 3 motes spent. Exalted targets (and other beings capable of channeling Essence) cannot have their Strength reduced below their permanent Essence with this Charm. Additionally, magical victims can cancel their weakness by spending 5 motes to concentrate, although this resistance counts as a defensive action. This Charm has no effect on targets whose permanent Essence is higher than the Abyssal's. Non-magical targets are not so lucky, however. If their Strength is reduced to zero, they remain Strength 1 for the rest of the scene, but they also lose a permanent dot of Strength that can only be recovered with experience. This Charm cannot permanently reduce a victim's Strength below 1.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Athletics tree, p. 204 (PDF 205).

name: Strength Stealing Technique
summary: With this Charm, an Abyssal can rob a living victim of her potency and add it to her own in hand-to-hand combat via a successful strike and a Willpower contest.
requirements: Minimum Athletics 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Infirmity Inflicting Gesture.
mechanics: With this Charm, an Abyssal can rob a living victim of her potency and add it to her own in hand-to-hand combat. The character must successfully strike the victim of this damage; her player makes a Willpower roll against the target's permanent Essence. If the Abyssal's player wins, the victim loses 1 dot of Strength for every 4 motes the Abyssal spent (according to the same rules as Infirmity Inflicting Gesture). In addition, the character gains 1 dot of Strength for reducing a mortal's rating and cannot have more than double his unmodified rating with this Charm. Victims regain all lost Strength rating at the end of the scene unless the rating was permanently reduced. As with Infirmity Inflicting Gesture, mortal crippled by the Charm cannot recover except by spending experience.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Athletics tree, pp. 204-205 (PDF 205-206). Closes out the Athletics tree (12 Charms total).

name: Fivefold Sensory Exercise
summary: Root of the Day Caste Awareness tree; guiding and expanding his perception with a rush of Essence, the character experiences every sensation magnified fivefold.
requirements: Minimum Awareness 2; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: Guiding and expanding his perception with a rush of Essence, a character with this Charm experiences every sensation magnified fivefold. Colors are deeper and richer, sounds more melodic or discordant, and scents somehow fuller and yet subtler at once. The world is achingly beautiful to the Abyssal, a painful realization indeed for those chosen to extinguish that beauty and drown it in the Void. In addition to adding his Essence to all Awareness rolls, the character employing this Charm can differentiate sensations far more readily than any mortal. It is incumbent upon the Storyteller to relay information accordingly. Characters using this Charm are no more susceptible to sensory overload than normal.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Awareness tree, root Charm, p. 204 (PDF 205).

name: Sense-Eroding Gesture
summary: With this Charm, a character with this Charm may dull an enemy's Awareness with a savage clawing motion, reducing all the target's Awareness dice pools by one die per success rolled.
requirements: Minimum Awareness 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Fivefold Sensory Exercise.
mechanics: With a savage clawing motion, a character with this Charm may dull an enemy's Awareness. The Abyssal's player rolls Manipulation + Awareness against a difficulty of the target's permanent Essence. Each success allows the Abyssal to reduce all the target's Awareness dice pools by one die for the duration of the Charm. This Charm cannot reduce a victim's dice pool lower than his Essence score. At the Storyteller's discretion, this penalty may also apply to other tasks requiring precise sensory acuity, such as Archery attacks. The Essence cost of this Charm must be paid prior to the activation roll.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Awareness tree, p. 204 (PDF 205).

name: Ominous Portent Method
summary: The character gains a 'sixth sense' that warns her whenever immediate danger threatens; the premonition drains 1 mote and cannot be placed in a Combo, but is fallible against purely spiritual or mental danger.
requirements: Minimum Awareness 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Fivefold Sensory Exercise.
mechanics: The character gains a 'sixth sense' that warns her whenever immediate danger threatens. Such premonitions require no roll, but the accompanying wave of horror drains 1 mote from the Abyssal. Experiencing a premonition does not count as a Charm use, allowing the Exalt to freely invoke other Charms on the same turn he receives a warning, but Ominous Portent Method cannot be placed in a Combo. The character's prescience warns her of any physical threat, from a concealed pit of spikes to an assassin's knife, but the Charm is not infallible and does nothing to warn of purely spiritual or mental danger.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Awareness tree, p. 205 (PDF 206).

name: Superior (Sense) Focus
summary: This Charm precisely duplicates the effects of the Solar Charm Keen (Sense) Technique; characters may use Superior (Sense) Focus in conjunction with Fivefold Sensory Exercise, and it manifests as Superior Sight Technique in the printed tree diagram.
requirements: Minimum Awareness 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Fivefold Sensory Exercise.
mechanics: This Charm precisely duplicates the effects of the Solar Charm Keen (Sense) Technique (see Exalted, p. 196). Characters may use Superior (Sense) Focus in conjunction with Fivefold Sensory Exercise. Once an Abyssal purchases this Charm for Sight (as Superior Sight Technique), he can thereafter see in darkness without penalty; enhanced vision pierces all shades of gloom, from moonlit night to the utter blackness of the Labyrinth. However, this modification also makes the character sensitive to bright light. Under lighting comparable to the noonday sun or close proximity to a torch, the Abyssal suffers the penalty for murky vision. The Exalt can suppress or reactivate his vision at will to avoid this problem, but each change takes one full turn and costs 1 mote. This change counts as a Charm, cannot be placed in a Combo, and leaves the character totally blind (-4 dice to attacks) during the turn it happens.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Awareness tree, p. 205-206 (PDF 206-207). The printed sub-tree diagram labels the Sight-specific purchase 'Superior Sight Technique'; text write-up uses the generic '(Sense)' template shared across senses.

name: Owl Eyes Treatment
summary: Once an Abyssal purchases Superior (Sense) Focus for Sight, he can thereafter see in darkness without penalty, though this makes him sensitive to bright light unless he suppresses the vision.
requirements: Minimum Awareness 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Superior Sight Focus (Superior (Sense) Focus, Sight).
mechanics: Once an Abyssal purchases this Charm, he can thereafter see in darkness without penalty. His enhanced vision pierces all shades of gloom, from moonlit night to the utter blackness of the Labyrinth. However, this modification also makes the character sensitive to bright light. Under lighting comparable to the noonday sun or close proximity to a torch, the Abyssal suffers the penalty for murky vision. The Exalt can suppress or reactivate his vision at will to avoid this problem, but each change takes one full turn and costs 1 mote. This change counts as a Charm (cannot be placed in a Combo) and leaves the character totally blind (-4 dice to attacks) during the turn it happens. This Charm does not allow the character to see more easily through fog or smoke, nor does it help him perceive invisible objects or people.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Awareness tree, p. 205 (PDF 206).

name: Incomparable (Sense) Technique
summary: This Charm precisely duplicates the effects of the Solar Charm Unsurpassed (Sense) Technique; characters may only learn permutations of this Charm to enhance senses they have already purchased with Superior (Sense) Focus, and it is incompatible with Superior (Sense) Focus and Fivefold Sensory Exercise.
requirements: Minimum Awareness 5; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Superior (Sense) Focus.
mechanics: This Charm precisely duplicates the effects of the Solar Charm Unsurpassed (Sense) Technique (see Exalted, p. 196). Characters may only learn permutations of this Charm to enhance senses they have already purchased with Superior (Sense) Focus. Incomparable (Sense) Technique is incompatible with Superior (Sense) Focus and Fivefold Sensory Exercise.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Awareness tree, p. 205 (PDF 206). Closes out the Awareness tree (6 Charms total).

name: Flitting Shadow Form
summary: Root of the Day Caste Dodge tree; the Exalt channels Essence through his body and movements, making him extremely difficult to strike, reducing the dice pool of a single attack by two dice per mote spent.
requirements: Minimum Dodge 2; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: The Exalt channels Essence through his body and movements, making him extremely difficult to strike. For every mote spent, the Abyssal reduces the dice pool of a single attack roll by two dice. This Charm can only target attacks aimed specifically at the Exalt and may reduce a dice pool to zero (ensuring that the attack misses). Characters may activate this Charm any time after an attack is declared but before dice are rolled. Flitting Shadow Form can only target attacks the Exalt is aware of.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Dodge tree, root Charm, p. 206 (PDF 207).

name: Uncanny Impulse Evasion
summary: Whenever a character with this Charm is attacked, she feels a sense of impending dread and may attempt to sidestep an unseen blow on instinct alone, with a dodge pool equal to her unmodified Dexterity.
requirements: Minimum Dodge 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Flitting Shadow Form.
mechanics: Whenever a character with this Charm is attacked, she feels a sense of impending dread and may attempt to sidestep an unseen blow on instinct alone. The character's dice pool for such a dodge equals her unmodified Dexterity. This Charm cannot be placed in a Combo with other Dodge Charms. If a deathknight's player does not choose to activate this Charm in response to an unseen attack, the Exalt does not sense the blow until it lands. This Charm must be activated prior to the attack roll.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Dodge tree, p. 206 (PDF 207).

name: Fivefold Shadow Form
summary: Moving faster than the shadows cast by a guttering candle, the Abyssal may evade blows with supernatural prowess, reducing the attacker's dice pool for a single attack by a number of dice equal to her Dodge + Essence.
requirements: Minimum Dodge 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Flitting Shadow Form.
mechanics: Moving faster than the shadows cast by a guttering candle, the Abyssal may evade blows with supernatural prowess. The attacker loses a number of dice from a single attack roll equal to the deathknight's Dodge + Essence. If this reduces the attack dice pool to zero, the blow automatically misses. This Charm must be activated prior to the attack roll.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Dodge tree, p. 206 (PDF 207).

name: Flickering Wisp Technique
summary: The Abyssal ripples and vanishes like smoke in a stiff breeze, coalescing a split second later a short distance away, perfectly dodging any one attack she can perceive without a roll, including magical effects that don't explicitly prohibit dodging.
requirements: Minimum Dodge 5; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Fivefold Shadow Form.
mechanics: The Abyssal ripples and vanishes like smoke in a stiff breeze, coalescing a split second later a short distance away. This Charm allows the character to perfectly dodge any one attack that he can perceive without a roll, including those without a roll, including those without a roll. The character still cannot dodge magical effects that explicitly prohibit dodging. The character may not move more yards with this technique than his permanent Essence rating and cannot use the Charm to teleport through solid barriers. Flickering Wisp Technique must be activated prior to the attack roll.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Dodge tree, p. 207 (PDF 208).

name: Incomparable Phantom Form
summary: Suffusing his body with spectral Essence, the Abyssal becomes translucent and partially dematerialized, ensuring that he can dodge all incoming attacks, perceived or otherwise, with his full Dexterity + Dodge pool.
requirements: Minimum Dodge 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Uncanny Impulse Evasion, Flickering Wisp Technique.
mechanics: Suffusing his body with spectral Essence, the Abyssal becomes translucent and partially dematerialized. In addition to unnerving opponents, this transformation allows the Exalt to dodge all incoming attacks, perceived or otherwise, with his full Dexterity + Dodge pool.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Dodge tree, p. 207 (PDF 208).

name: Flowing Evasion Assault
summary: In addition to teleporting out of harm's way, an Abyssal with this Charm can ensure that she materializes behind her opponent, following the same rules as Flickering Wisp Technique with two extra exceptions, and gaining a free attack from behind.
requirements: Minimum Dodge 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Flickering Wisp Technique.
mechanics: In addition to teleporting out of harm's way, an Abyssal with this Charm can ensure that she materializes behind her opponent. Flowing Evasion Assault follows the same rules as Flickering Wisp Technique with two exceptions. First, the Exalt may reappear as far away as her Dodge in yards. Secondly, if the attacker is within that range, the Abyssal may automatically reappear behind her target. If the Abyssal has any actions remaining to launch an attack of her own, she gains the full benefits of attacking from behind (see Exalted, p. 238).
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Dodge tree, pp. 207-208 (PDF 208-209). Closes out the Dodge tree (6 Charms total).

name: Theft of Face
summary: Root of the first Day Caste Larceny branch; by stealing a victim's Essence, a character with this Charm can also steal her visage, becoming her perfect likeness after an hour of meditation.
requirements: Minimum Larceny 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: By stealing a victim's Essence, a character with this Charm can also steal her visage. The character must completely drain her victim of blood and spend one hour digesting and studying the stolen Essence. At the conclusion of her meditation, the Exalt shifts into the perfect likeness of her victim. This is not an illusion, but a startling transformation. Every mark and scar is duplicated, and every tic and mannerism compensated for. If questioned, the Exalt can even draw on the stolen memories of her prey with an Intelligence + Larceny roll at a difficulty assigned by the Storyteller. No amount of physical scrutiny can discern that the Abyssal is not whom she pretends to be, although an Abyssal anima victims who are the same gender as the Exalt. Although she may disguise herself as an Exalted victim and even duplicate the powers or anima of an Solar or Lunar scarring, the character cannot emulate the powers or anima of an Exalted victim, but this is not applied. Once the character voluntarily ends this Charm, she loses all memories and shifts back to her true form. Death also ends the ruse. Characters can only assume a given guise once before the memories are digested.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Larceny tree, root Charm, p. 207 (PDF 208).

name: Theft of Mien
summary: This Charm duplicates the effects of Theft of Face with one exception: the Exalt also steals intuitive knowledge of her victim's mannerisms and habits, making the ruse much more effective, though close family members can still recognize odd behavior.
requirements: Minimum Larceny 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Theft of Face.
mechanics: This Charm duplicates the effects of Theft of Face with one exception: the Exalt also steals intuitive knowledge of her victim's mannerisms and habits. Consequently, the ruse is much more effective and can easily fool casual associates of the target. Close family members can still recognize that something is wrong, regardless of whether they actually suspect an imposter or attribute the odd behavior to illness.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Larceny tree, p. 208 (PDF 209).

name: Flawless Doppelganger Disguise
summary: This Charm holds the same effects as Theft of Mien, but the disguise persists until the Exalt releases it rather than expiring after an hour.
requirements: Minimum Larceny 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Theft of Mien.
mechanics: This Charm holds the same effects as Theft of Mien, but the disguise persists until the Exalt releases it rather than expiring automatically.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Larceny tree, p. 208 (PDF 209).

name: Solar Impersonation Style
summary: By channeling the nascent spark of Solar Essence trapped within her, an Abyssal with this Charm can shift her anima to resemble that of a Chosen of the Unconquered Sun for a day, deceiving all but Zenith Solars or Night Caste with the same technique.
requirements: Minimum Larceny 5; Minimum Essence 4; Prerequisite Charms: Flawless Doppelganger Disguise.
mechanics: By channeling the nascent spark of Solar Essence trapped within her, an Abyssal with this Charm can shift her anima to resemble that of a Chosen of the Unconquered Sun. While this Charm is in effect, the deathknight's anima banner and Caste Mark manifest exactly as a Solar of the appropriate type (Dusk becomes Dawn, Midnight becomes Zenith, etc.). This Charm only affects the anima banner, however. The Exalt retains her true power appropriate to her true Caste. Any Zenith Caste Solar with a Permanent Essence higher than the Abyssal's can see through the disguise. Only Abyssal Exalted may learn this Charm, although it is rumored that some Solars of the Night Caste may have developed a similar technique for impersonating deathknights.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Larceny tree, pp. 208-209 (PDF 209-210). Closes out the first (Theft of Face) Larceny sub-branch.

name: Cunning Criminal Style
summary: Root of the second Day Caste Larceny branch; many criminals live short, bleak lives, and an Abyssal who taps into the shared regrets and suffering of the dead has a wealth of information at his disposal about local crime networks.
requirements: Minimum Larceny 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: Many criminals live short lives and die just as bleakly. Accordingly, an Abyssal who taps into the shared regrets and suffering of the dead has a wealth of information at his disposal. He can intuitively pick out criminal establishments from honest businesses and discern those who actively desire to sell or buy illegal merchandise. Just as easily, the Abyssal can spot the lines of power in the local crime scene and track them back to the true crime-lords of the area. While this Charm remains active, the character remains at home in any criminal subculture. Cunning Criminal Style cannot discern informers or undercover agents from ordinary criminals unless there are sufficient clues present to draw such a conclusion.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Larceny tree, p. 209 (PDF 210).

name: Evidence-Erasing Method
summary: With this Charm active, an Abyssal leaves no more evidence of her passing than as she usually would, but she does not drop unintentional clues such as footprints, hair, etc. unless she chooses to.
requirements: Minimum Larceny 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Cunning Criminal Style.
mechanics: With this Charm active, an Abyssal leaves no more evidence of her passing than she usually would, but she does not drop unintentional clues such as footprints, hair, etc. Obviously, if an Abyssal wants to leave evidence such as physical evidence such as footprints, hair, etc, she may do so, since the Charm only protects against unintentional evidence. Only supernatural tracking can find a character shrouded with this Charm.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Larceny tree, p. 209 (PDF 210).

name: Lock-Weathering Touch
summary: With this Charm, an Exalt can instantly bypass any mundane lock with a gentle touch; the lock rusts inside with a wisp of acrid smoke, causing the mechanism to fall open.
requirements: Minimum Larceny 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Cunning Criminal Style.
mechanics: With this Charm, an Exalt can instantly bypass any mundane lock with a gentle touch. The lock rusts inside with a wisp of acrid smoke, causing the mechanism to fall open. This Charm must be used separately on each lock and may affect locked manacles as easily as the bolts of doors or safes.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Larceny tree, p. 209 (PDF 210).

name: Artful Conjuration Trick
summary: Through the use of this Charm, an Abyssal becomes preternaturally deft at sleight of hand and may perform amazing feats of conjuration and legerdemain without requiring a roll, palming a coin from a pouch or instantly palming a handful of shuriken.
requirements: Minimum Larceny 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Evidence-Erasing Method, Lock-Weathering Touch.
mechanics: Through the use of this Charm, an Abyssal becomes preternaturally deft at sleight of hand and may perform amazing feats of conjuration and legerdemain without requiring a roll. For outright impossible stunts, such as actually summoning a coin from a belt pouch without reaching for it, the Storyteller may require a Dexterity + Larceny roll. This Charm is intended for trickery and bedazzlement, not combat. Instantly palming a handful of shuriken is permissible, but the Charm cannot actually create something from nothing, nor steal possessions from an opponent. The Storyteller retains final say on what can and cannot be done with this Charm.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Larceny tree, p. 210 (PDF 211).

name: Striking Snake Grab
summary: Capstone of the second Day Caste Larceny branch, building on the sleight-of-hand mastery of Artful Conjuration Trick to permit outright theft of items from a target.
requirements: Minimum Larceny 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Artful Conjuration Trick.
mechanics: This Charm's full effect text was not captured with sufficient confidence in this extraction pass; the Charm's header, cost, duration, type, and prerequisite were confirmed directly from the printed page, but the descriptive rules paragraph should be re-verified against the source before promotion.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Larceny tree, p. 210 (PDF 211). Closes out the Larceny tree (9 Charms total). Full rules text flagged for a follow-up close read before promotion.

name: Concealing Distraction Discipline
summary: Root of the Day Caste Stealth tree; briefly eroding the attention span of onlookers with a gentle rush of Essence, an Abyssal with this Charm becomes far more difficult to notice until she draws attention or is spotted.
requirements: Minimum Stealth 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: Briefly eroding the attention span of onlookers with a gentle rush of Essence, an Abyssal with this Charm becomes far more difficult to notice. Until the end of the scene, all attempts to spot the Exalt increase their difficulty by his permanent Essence. This increase applies only so long as the Abyssal does not draw undue attention to himself and remains unnoticed. If he is spotted by anyone, the Charm immediately ends and cannot be reactivated until the Exalt moves entirely out of sight.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Stealth tree, root Charm, p. 210 (PDF 211).

name: Encounter-Banishing Gesture
summary: Despite their prowess, even the most stealthy and nimble Day Castes get caught from time to time; with this Charm, a character can rip the memory of an encounter from a target's mind so that he forgets he ever saw the Exalt.
requirements: Minimum Stealth 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Concealing Distraction Discipline.
mechanics: Despite their prowess, even the most stealthy and nimble Day Castes get caught from time to time. With this Charm, a character can rip the memory of an encounter from a target's mind so that he forgets he ever saw the Exalt. The Abyssal's player rolls Manipulation + Stealth against a difficulty of the target's Essence (or highest Essence in the case of a group). For every success rolled, the target forgets the events of that turn. Thus, four successes erase the past four turns of a target's memory. As an added benefit, a befuddled target will not notice the Abyssal again for a like number of turns unless she draws attention to herself again for a while longer. This gives the Exalt a few seconds to escape and conceal herself more thoroughly. This Charm has no effect on beings with a higher permanent Essence than the Abyssal or against beings who are physically agitated (for example, those in combat).
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Stealth tree, p. 211 (PDF 212).

name: Splinter in the Mind's Eye
summary: This Charm duplicates the effects and rules of Encounter-Banishing Gesture, except that its effects extend to a number of witnesses equal to the Abyssal's Essence rating x 10 without requiring more motes for each observer.
requirements: Minimum Stealth 5; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Encounter-Banishing Gesture.
mechanics: This Charm duplicates the effects and rules of Encounter-Banishing Gesture, except that its effects extend to a number of witnesses equal to the Abyssal's Essence rating x 10 without requiring more motes for each observer.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Stealth tree, p. 211 (PDF 212).

name: Noiseless Phantom Style
summary: Enveloped in the stillness of the grave, an Abyssal with this Charm makes no noise -- her footsteps do not echo or splash, and she can jump or stomp in perfect eerie silence, though her voice and magic still work normally.
requirements: Minimum Stealth 4; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Concealing Distraction Discipline.
mechanics: Enveloped in the stillness of the grave, an Abyssal with this Charm makes no noise. Her footsteps do not echo or splash, and she can jump or stomp in perfect eerie silence. Conversely, she cannot speak or employ any magic that relies on sound. This Charm only works against sounds made by the character, however. Her blade might slice soundlessly through a victim's ribs, but the effect would not muffle the victim's scream of pain or rasping death rattle.
compatibility: Duration: Stealth in minutes. Type: Reflexive.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Stealth tree, p. 212 (PDF 213).

name: Stifled Cry Exercise
summary: The Abyssal focuses on a single victim within line of sight and smothers his voice with Essence; until the end of the turn the target cannot speak or make any other vocalized noise, useful for Day Caste assassins to prevent victims from screaming.
requirements: Minimum Stealth 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Noiseless Phantom Style.
mechanics: The character focuses on a single victim within line of sight and smothers his voice with Essence. Until the end of the turn, the target cannot speak or make any other vocalized noise. Day Caste assassins often employ this Charm to prevent their victims from screaming. This Charm has no effect on beings with a higher permanent Essence than the Abyssal.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Stealth tree, p. 212 (PDF 213).

name: Shadow Cloak Technique
summary: The Abyssal cocoons himself in pure darkness, taking on the wraithlike appearance of a solidified shadow; so long as he remains in darkness or among other shadows, he adds 1 die per 2 motes spent to all Stealth rolls.
requirements: Minimum Stealth 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Noiseless Phantom Style.
mechanics: The Abyssal cocoons himself in pure darkness, taking on the wraithlike appearance of a solidified shadow. So long as he remains in darkness or among other shadows, he adds 1 die per 2 motes spent to all Stealth rolls. The Exalt cannot purchase more dice with this Charm than twice his Essence rating. If a bright light is shined on the hidden Exalt, his cloak dissolves immediately, and the Charm ends.
compatibility: Duration: Stealth in turns. Type: Simple.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Stealth tree, p. 212 (PDF 213).

name: Unseen Wisp Method
summary: The Abyssal vanishes wholly from sight, dissolving in a ripple of scattering shadows; ranged attacks against her are all but impossible without magical aid or well-directed stunts.
requirements: Minimum Stealth 5; Minimum Essence 4; Prerequisite Charms: Concealing Distraction Discipline.
mechanics: The Abyssal vanishes wholly from sight, dissolving in a ripple of scattering shadows. For a number of turns equal to half the number of motes invested, the Exalt is nothing more than a wavering blur in the air. Ranged attacks against her are all but impossible without magical aid or well-directed stunts, while close-range attacks suffer a difficulty penalty of the deathknight's permanent Essence.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Day Caste Stealth tree, p. 212 (PDF 213). Closes out the Stealth tree (7 Charms) and, with it, all five Day Caste Charm trees (Athletics, Awareness, Dodge, Larceny, Stealth).

name: Authority-Eroding Technique
summary: Root of one Moonshadow Caste Bureaucracy branch; through this Charm, an Abyssal can momentarily confuse a target and weaken her effectiveness in a critical moment, reducing her dice pool for a single Bureaucracy roll.
requirements: Minimum Bureaucracy 1; Minimum Essence 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: Through this Charm, an Abyssal can momentarily confuse a target and weaken her effectiveness in a critical moment. For every mote spent, the target loses one die from a single Bureaucracy roll. This Charm cannot reduce a victim's dice pool lower than her Essence. Authority-Eroding Technique may be invoked any time after an appropriate action is declared but before dice are rolled. The Abyssal can even set up the targeted roll, as by asking a pointed question in a meeting.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Bureaucracy tree, root Charm, p. 212 (PDF 213).

name: Argument-Slaying Remark
summary: By speaking brusquely and projecting an aura of menace, an Abyssal with this Charm can cut through the drawn-out process of debate, ending an argument within moments with the best resolution the target could have achieved through continued discussion.
requirements: Minimum Bureaucracy 2; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Authority-Eroding Technique.
mechanics: By speaking brusquely and projecting an aura of menace, an Abyssal with this Charm can cut through the drawn-out process of debate. The targeted argument ends within moments with the best resolution the target could have achieved with continued discussion. For example, a character could use this Charm to derive the best price from a merchant, saving minutes or perhaps even hours of haggling. Note that Argument-Slaying Remark isn't a perfect 'final word' Charm -- if an answer would be no regardless of what the Abyssal might say or argue, then the answer remains no. This Charm simply brings the matter to a conclusion instantly.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Bureaucracy tree, pp. 212-213 (PDF 213-214).

name: Alluring Eloquence Method
summary: This Charm allows an Exalt to vocalize a course of action or point of view with such eloquence and grace that opponents find it difficult or even impossible to argue, resisted by a Bureaucracy or Performance roll augmented with the deathknight's Essence rating.
requirements: Minimum Bureaucracy 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Argument-Slaying Remark.
mechanics: This Charm allows an Exalt to vocalize a course of action or point of view with such eloquence and grace that opponents find it difficult or even impossible to argue. The Abyssal's player makes the Bureaucracy or Performance roll as normal, but all rivals add the deathknight's Essence rating to their countarguments.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Bureaucracy tree, p. 213 (PDF 214).

name: Corruption-Sensing Scrutiny
summary: Root of the second Moonshadow Caste Bureaucracy branch; with this Charm, an Abyssal can perceive corrupt officials and bureaucrats by a distinctive oily stain on their aura, or intuitively gauge a clean official's susceptibility to corruption.
requirements: Minimum Bureaucracy 2; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: With this Charm, an Abyssal can perceive corrupt officials and bureaucrats by a distinctive oily stain on their aura. Alternately, she can intuitively gauge a 'clean' official's susceptibility to corruption. Her player rolls Perception + Bureaucracy against a difficulty of the target's Essence score. The amount of information gleaned depends on the number of successes rolled. Simple success allows the Abyssal to sense whether the target has ever engaged in corruption or not (i.e., accepted a bribe, doctored a report, etc.). With three successes, the character can measure the depth of a target's corruption or her overall vulnerability to such. Thus, she can distinguish the minor blotches of a plagiarizing poet who secretly assassinated his rivals. With five successes, the Abyssal gains a vague sense of the target's offenses, though without the context or specifics. This hunch enables the deathknight to take advantage of a hidden official's weakness or vice -- or simply to know whom best to bribe.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Bureaucracy tree, p. 212 (PDF 213).

name: Cunning Subversion Style
summary: With a few artfully placed rumors and whispers, an Abyssal with this Charm can sow the seeds of discord and mistrust within a particular bureau or organization, causing it to grind to a halt and factionalism.
requirements: Minimum Bureaucracy 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Corruption-Sensing Scrutiny.
mechanics: With a few artfully placed rumors and whispers, an Abyssal with this Charm can sow the seeds of discord and mistrust within a particular bureau or organization. Tempers flare, growing mistrust leads to outright hostility and factionalism; the bureau steadily grinds to a halt and implodes under the weight of indolence and excess. This Charm can fully affect a department whose total membership is no greater than the deathknight's Essence rating x 20. If the character wishes to affect a larger organization, he must use this Charm multiple times or settle for a slower, less effect one at random. Regardless, it takes time for infighting and paranoia to build to an extent that it actually impedes efficiency. While this is left to Storytellers to adjudicate, the overall corruption and rivalry effect plays a significant role, as does the quality and strength of leadership within the organization. Generally, this Charm is beyond the scope of rules and has little tangible effect. Its intangible effects can be quite dramatic, however. Few organizations with mortal total members can withstand more than a month of this Charm without utterly disintegrating.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Bureaucracy tree, pp. 212-213 (PDF 213-214).

name: Regime-Toppling Insinuation
summary: This Charm closely parallels Cunning Subversion Style, but rather than targeting an organization, the Abyssal focuses her havoc against a specific leader, making his orders morose or disregarded by subordinates.
requirements: Minimum Bureaucracy 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Cunning Subversion Style.
mechanics: This Charm closely parallels Cunning Subversion Style, however, the Abyssal may focus the havoc against a specific leader. If there is no actual coup or assassination attempt -- though there might be -- the concomitant treachery and distrust makes all but the most tyrannical control ineffective. The victim's orders are twisted or disregarded by subordinates, while overall morale drops to an all-time low. Each application of this Charm may permanently affect a number of people equal to the character's Essence rating x 20. As with Cunning Subversion Style, this Charm is primarily a matter of roleplaying rather than rules. Still, it is unlikely that any mortal leader can last more than a month with a hierarchy under his control full of hatred and mistrust toward him. Whether he is pushed out of office or stabbed to death in an alley depends very much on the nature of the victim's subordinates and the type of organization. Ironically, true tyrants have little to fear from negative popular opinion, as they already know how to retain authority in the face of a widespread hierarchy.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Bureaucracy tree, p. 213 (PDF 214).

name: Iron Tyrant Mien
summary: Exuding menace and prowess in equal measure, an Abyssal can enchant his authority to sow fear and discourage rebellion; while active, individuals with a Willpower rating lower than the character's cannot organize rebellion against him.
requirements: Minimum Bureaucracy 5; Minimum Essence 4; Prerequisite Charms: Alluring Eloquence Method, Regime-Toppling Insinuation.
mechanics: Exuding menace and prowess in equal measure, an Abyssal can enchant his authority to sow fear and discourage rebellion. The character must have some recognized leadership position in order to use this Charm, although the type and scope of leadership doesn't matter. A caravan master can surpass a king in brutal tyranny. While this Charm is active, no one with a Willpower score lower than the character's Essence rating may act against the deathknight's authority, let alone participate in outright rebellion. Individuals with a Willpower rating equal to the character's Willpower may act against the despot, but her players suffer a difficulty increase of the character's permanent Essence on all Social rolls to rally others to the cause. Characters whose Willpower exceeds the Abyssal's are, as always, immune to this Charm, as are all magical beings. Also, this Charm only affects members of the hierarchy over which the Exalt presides. A great monarch could order any subject about but would have no authority over a foreign citizen. Storyteller discretion is particularly important in preventing abuse of this Charm. Of course, a large sphere of influence carries its own risks. Besides the likelihood that a strong-willed champion will organize a coup, corrupt tyrants also attract jealous rivals who wish to usurp their power.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Bureaucracy tree, p. 213 (PDF 214). Closes out the Bureaucracy tree (7 Charms total).

name: Language Absorbing Method
summary: Root of one Moonshadow Caste Linguistics branch; with this Charm, an Abyssal may absorb a victim's knowledge of language even as he devours her Essence, so that the deathknight speaks the tongue with perfect fluency and no trace of accent.
requirements: Minimum Linguistics 2; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: With this Charm, an Abyssal may absorb a victim's knowledge of language even as he devours her Essence. The character must have consumed at least 1 mote from the target sometime during the scene -- whether through blood drinking, Charms, etc. His player rolls Wits + Linguistics, with a difficulty of (5 - the total number of motes taken). If this lowers the difficulty below 0, no roll is needed. If the roll succeeds, the Abyssal instantly knows one language of his choice known to the target. This knowledge is absolute -- the deathknight speaks with perfect fluency and no trace of accent and may read and write in the tongue so long as the target knew how to do so. If the character consumes more than 5 motes, he may spend double the requisite experience point to digest his stolen linguistics knowledge and permanently increase his Linguistics rating on the spot. Otherwise, languages absorbed with this Charm fade completely when the Charm expires.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Linguistics tree, root Charm, pp. 213-214 (PDF 214-215).

name: Peerless Fluency Style
summary: As the warrior-poets of the Underworld, many Abyssal Exalted speak and write with haunting skill and eloquence; for every mote spent, the character may add one die to all Linguistics rolls for a specific known language.
requirements: Minimum Linguistics 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Language Absorbing Method.
mechanics: As the warrior-poets of the Underworld, many Abyssal Exalted speak and write with haunting skill and eloquence. For every mote spent on this Charm, the character may add one die to all Linguistics rolls for a specific known language. These dice are mechanically identical to a Linguistics specialty (see Exalted, p. 140) and may similarly add to other communication-related rolls, at Storyteller discretion. The character cannot purchase more bonus dice for any language than her Intelligence score. Note that characters with four or more dice of fluency convey superhuman grace, is immediately evident to any listener or reader. Indeed, slow-witted mortals may have trouble following the cadence and intricate vocabulary of such characters.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Linguistics tree, p. 214 (PDF 215).

name: Theft of Words
summary: With this Charm, an Abyssal can temporarily excise a victim's comprehension of a particular language, indicating a target within line of sight and whispering softly to strip their understanding.
requirements: Minimum Linguistics 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Language Absorbing Method.
mechanics: With this Charm, an Abyssal can temporarily excise a victim's comprehension of a particular language. The Exalt whispers softly in the maddening dialect of the Malfeans and indicates a target within line of sight. His player then rolls Manipulation + Linguistics against a difficulty of the target's permanent Essence. For every success rolled, the character may spend 5 motes to remove a random language or pick a language known by the Abyssal and suppress it. The latter is a gamble, however, unless the Exalt is certain his target knows the language in question. Individuals deprived of all languages cannot speak or write at all, although they may attempt to grunt and crudely pantomime their intentions. Once the duration ends, the target regains full memory of all her forgotten languages. This Charm has no effect on beings with a higher permanent Essence than the Exalt.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Linguistics tree, p. 214 (PDF 215).

name: Confusion of Tongues
summary: Cursing sharply in the lost tongue of the Malfeans, the Abyssal distorts all communication in a zone around her; no one inside this area of effect can understand written or spoken language.
requirements: Minimum Linguistics 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Theft of Words.
mechanics: Cursing sharply in the lost tongue of the Malfeans, the Abyssal distorts all communication in a zone around her. No one inside this area of effect can understand written or spoken language. Familiar letters run together into baffling glyphs, while every spoken phrase twists into complete gibberish. Clever characters can still communicate simple concepts via pantomime or crude drawings, but formal or established hand signs convey no more meaning than any spoken tongue. The character makes a Manipulation + Linguistics roll against the targets, with a difficulty equal to the targets' highest permanent Essence. This Charm has no effect on beings whose permanent Essence matches or exceeds the Abyssal's. However, while such beings hear and see languages as they truly are, their own words remain twisted to affected beings. The zone of distortion extends to a radius of (the character's permanent Essence x 3) yards. With vocalized speech, neither party projects information as they truly intend to convey. This Charm does not allow deeper mind reading or memory probing, nor does it preclude deception.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Linguistics tree, pp. 214-215 (PDF 215-216).

name: Words Beneath a Whisper
summary: An Abyssal with this Charm may communicate telepathically with anyone she knows to invoke this Charm, projecting thoughts at will as a reflexive action to speak with someone she does not share a language with.
requirements: Minimum Linguistics 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Theft of Words.
mechanics: An Abyssal with this Charm may communicate entirely telepathically with anyone she knows to invoke this Charm. The character must be able to directly sense her target to invoke this Charm. If at any time the Exalt cannot perceive her target, the connection instantly breaks, and the Charm ends. While the link remains, the Abyssal can project her thoughts at will as a reflexive action, enabling her to speak with someone she does not share a language with. The target knows the thoughts come from outside his mind, although he cannot pinpoint their source without other magic unless the Exalt identifies herself. Similarly, the target may project his own thoughts and replies along the link. As with vocalized speech, neither party projects information they do not intend to convey. This Charm does not allow deeper mind reading or memory probing, nor does it preclude deception.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Linguistics tree, pp. 215-216 (PDF 216-217).

name: Blood Inscription Technique
summary: Root of the second Moonshadow Caste Linguistics branch; by channeling Essence-laden blood through his fingertips, an Exalt with this Charm knows his writing always makes marks resembling tattoos that gradually fade over days or weeks like applied dye.
requirements: Minimum Linguistics 1; Minimum Essence 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: By channeling Essence-laden blood through his fingertips, an Exalt with this Charm knows his writing always leaves marks. As the Abyssal traces glyphs with his fingers, his touch leaves marks of indelible crimson. Marks etched with this Charm are virtually indistinguishable from ink stains and can be cleaned or removed as if the writing surface permits. If used to mark living beings, the glyphs resemble tattoos, but gradually fade over a period of days or weeks like any applied dye. Characters using this Charm write with uncanny precision, easily matching the graceful calligraphy of even a very fine stylus or brush.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Linguistics tree, root Charm, p. 216 (PDF 217).

name: Ghost-Warding Glyph
summary: By tracing a mystical rune on a target's forehead, an Abyssal with this Charm may protect an individual from hungry ghosts and walking dead; the mark washes off after a day, and the Abyssal may use the Glyph on himself.
requirements: Minimum Linguistics 2; Minimum Occult 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Corpus-Rending Blow, Blood Inscription Technique.
mechanics: By tracing a mystical rune on a target's forehead, an Abyssal with this Charm may protect an individual from hungry ghosts and walking dead. The mark washes off and retains a slick appearance until after it dries. For the duration of the Charm, no zombie or bestial ghost will attack the target unless compelled to do so by a necromancer, an Abyssal, or some other supernatural compulsion. Sentient ghosts generally leave the character alone out of fear of the Deathlords but are not compelled to. This Charm has no effect on Exalted, but any display of an anima banner or Caste Mark burns off the rune and revokes the protection. The Abyssal may use the Ghost-Warding Glyph on himself.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Linguistics tree, p. 216 (PDF 217). Re-verified against a fresh render of printed p. 216 (PDF 217): the stat block reads 'Minimum Linguistics: 2 / Minimum Occult: 4 / Minimum Essence: 2 / Prerequisite Charms: Corpus-Rending Blow, Blood Inscription Technique' -- the 'Minimum Occult: 4' line was missed in the original transcription and has now been added above. RESOLVED: the prerequisite 'Corpus-Rending Blow' is the Daybreak Caste Occult-tree Charm now correctly catalogued under id corpus-rending-blow (p. 199/PDF 200) -- an earlier pass had mistranscribed that Charm's own name as 'Corpse-Rending Blow' and treated the two spellings as distinct, unresolved Charms. Both rows have been reconciled; see the corpus-rending-blow row's notes for the full resolution. This Charm is no longer blocked pending an unresolved prerequisite.

name: Corpus-Rending Blow
summary: Charging his hand or weapon with spectral energy, the character can make one strike against an immaterial spirit; a successful hit inflicts aggravated damage and drains Essence at the Abyssal's discretion.
requirements: Minimum Occult 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Spirit Sensing Technique.
mechanics: Charging his hand or weapon with spectral energy, the character can make one strike against an immaterial spirit. The character's player must still roll to hit the creature normally, although the deathknight may elect to attack the spirit's Essence in lieu of inflicting damage. This decision must be made before activating the Charm, before rolling the attack. If the Abyssal chooses to drain Essence, roll her Conviction + Occult using the spirit's Valor as its soak total. Each level of damage inflicted in this fashion drains 2 motes of Essence from the spirit's pool and adds it to the character's own. Drained motes that would take a character above her normal maximum are still drained but dissipate without benefit to the Exalt. If the character uses this Charm to cause actual damage, the attack is resolved normally. This Charm has no ability to perceive incorporeal spirits, so characters attacking without other magic (such as Spirit Sensing Technique) suffer the usual penalty for blind fighting. This Charm has no effect on materialized spirits. Corpus-Rending Blow is explicitly permitted to be part of a Combo with Charms of other Abilities.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Occult tree ('Occult 3'), p. 199 (PDF 200). Ghost-Warding Glyph is no longer blocked by an unresolved prerequisite.

name: Glyph-Unveiling Meditation
summary: By touching a sample of writing, an Abyssal with this Charm can attune his mind to the lingering wisps of memory left by the author, reading the tainted work with perfect fluency and comprehension.
requirements: Minimum Linguistics 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Blood Inscription Technique.
mechanics: By touching a sample of writing, an Abyssal with this Charm can attune his mind to the lingering wisps of memory left by the author. The Exalt can read the targeted work with perfect fluency, but loses attunement or comprehension as soon as he stops reading or reaches the end of the document. Note that it is not necessary to read in a linear manner; he may skim passages, jump ahead and reread sections as many times as desired. However, once the Abyssal halts to pursue another task, the Charm ends. Although an Exalt can quote specific passages or recall exact wording after the Charm ends, he will still remember what he read and what it meant. This Charm does not work against artificial languages, codes and other such methods of deliberately obscuring the content of a work, as the author's intent is devious and the traces left behind are opaque.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Linguistics tree, p. 216 (PDF 217).

name: Scathing Cynic Attitude
summary: A character using this Charm becomes preternaturally resistant to all forms of persuasion, from simple argument to outright mind control; her Nature changes to Critic for the duration.
requirements: Minimum Linguistics 5; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Peerless Fluency Style, Blood Inscription Technique.
mechanics: A character using this Charm becomes preternaturally resistant to all forms of persuasion, from simple argument to outright mind control. For the duration of the Charm, the character's Nature changes to Critic. Any time the deathknight is subjected to words of magic that would alter his point of view or perceptions, his player may reflexively roll Willpower against a difficulty equal to the offending character's Essence. Success allows the Abyssal to scornfully shrug off the suggestion. Characters using this Charm are notably brusque and bitter, which adds +1 to the difficulty of all Charisma rolls. Scathing Cynic Attitude cannot defend against persuasion by beings with a higher permanent Essence than the character's Willpower.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Linguistics tree, pp. 216-217 (PDF 217-218). Closes out the Linguistics tree (9 fully-verified Charms plus 1 unresolved placeholder for Corpus-Rending Blow; 10 rows total).

name: Soul Reins
summary: Root of the Moonshadow Caste Ride tree; a character with this Charm can subdue a mount with her supernatural will, reducing its Control Rating for every mote spent.
requirements: Minimum Ride 2; Minimum Essence 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: A character with this Charm can subdue a mount with her supernatural will. For every mote spent, the targeted animal has its Control Rating reduced by one point. If this reduces the steed's Control Rating to zero, it obeys unhesitatingly and will jump to its death if so directed. Mounts tamed with this Charm only obey the Exalt. All other characters must contend with the beast's normal Control Rating. Soul Reins only affects animals trained for riding -- characters cannot jump on the back of a wild tyrant lizard and expect compliance.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Ride tree, root Charm, p. 216 (PDF 217).

name: Mount-Breaking Method
summary: Similar to Soul Reins, this Charm allows an Exalt to dominate a steed and subsume its will to her own, permanently reducing the mount's Control Rating and granting immunity to terror when ridden by the Abyssal.
requirements: Minimum Ride 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Soul Reins.
mechanics: Similar to Soul Reins, this Charm allows a deathknight to dominate a steed and subsume its will to her own. Unlike the lesser Charm, however, the effects of Mount-Breaking Method are permanent. The character's player rolls Strength + Ride against a difficulty of the animal's Control Rating. Each success permanently reduces the mount's Control Rating by one point, to a minimum score of one. If the Abyssal's player actually rolls enough successes to reduce a Control Rating to zero, the beast gains immunity to terror when ridden by the Exalt. Although the final outcome is a foregone conclusion based on the results of the roll, the character must still spend the rest of the scene aggressively taming her steed. Unless this roll is botched, the Exalt will not suffer injury during the training session. The Charm actually weakens the core of the beast rather than simply compelling obedience, so the mount's new Control Rating applies to all riders. Mount-Breaking Method may affect any animal that can possibly be trained to accept a rider, even dangerous beasts such as hydroc or bear. The character must have a permanent Essence of 3 or higher to train exotic or deadly animals, however.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Ride tree, pp. 217-218 (PDF 218-219).

name: Tireless Charger Technique
summary: With this Charm, a mounted character can briefly sustain and push his steed with raw Essence, granting boundless energy at the cost of unsoakable lethal damage to the mount each hour it's maintained.
requirements: Minimum Ride 5; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Mount-Breaking Method.
mechanics: With this Charm, a mounted character can briefly sustain and push his steed with raw Essence. Tireless Charger Technique lasts until the Abyssal dismounts or a number of hours have passed equal to his Ride score. Enchanted steeds have boundless energy and never need to stop for food or water. The necrotic Essence powering this Charm also eats at the animal's life force. For every hour or fraction thereof that the Charm is maintained, the horse suffers one level of unsoakable lethal damage. This damage is deferred until the Charm ends. After a horse suffers from this Charm, it cannot be safely re-enchanted with this Charm until it fully heals its wounds. Doing otherwise allows the horse to act at full strength again, but immediately kills the mount when the forced march ends.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Ride tree, p. 217 (PDF 218).

name: Spectral Steed
summary: With this Charm, a character may summon a ghost horse from the Essence of the Underworld, materializing out of dusky smoke with the statistics of a war horse but tireless, fearless, and biting with an inflicted 4L bite.
requirements: Minimum Ride 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Forceful Spirit Spur.
mechanics: With this Charm, a character may summon a ghost horse from the Essence of the Underworld. Materializing out of dusky smoke, the beast has the appearance of a pure black stallion with eyes like smoldering coals and sharp teeth no horse alive should have. It has the same statistics as a war horse of excellent quality (see Exalted, p. 316), but it is utterly tireless, fearless and inflicts 4L with a successful bite. Spectral steeds do not need food or drink, but enjoy the taste of human flesh and blood. If a character drains this Charm again after its duration expires, a new horse appears, and the old one dissolves with a screaming whinny.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Ride tree, pp. 217-218 (PDF 218-219).

name: Forceful Spirit Spur
summary: An Abyssal with this Charm can silently summon her mount from great distances; the steed feels the bite of phantom spurs digging harshly into its flanks unless it moves at best possible speed toward the Exalt.
requirements: Minimum Ride 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Soul Reins.
mechanics: An Abyssal with this Charm can silently summon her mount from great distances. The steed feels the bite of phantom spurs digging harshly into her flanks unless it moves at best possible speed toward the Exalt. This Charm has a range of (the character's permanent Essence x 10) miles. The Abyssal must have clearly exerted dominance over the summoned animal before it will answer a summons. Such dominance can have been achieved through physical (such as beating or through rough use of a whip) or mystical (as in the case of Soul Reins) means. While animals under the influence of this Charm are distracted or become lost, they cannot circumvent complex obstacles any better than normal. The compulsion inflicted by this Charm remains in force until the animal reaches its master or moves beyond range.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Ride tree, p. 218 (PDF 219).

name: Mount-Spooking Shout
summary: The Abyssal pours Essence into his voice, unleashing an unholy shriek that terrifies most steeds; all living mounts within earshot must make a roll or rear and bolt unless pushed for short agonizing bursts by their rider.
requirements: Minimum Ride 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Soul Reins.
mechanics: The Abyssal pours Essence into his voice, unleashing an unholy shriek that terrifies most steeds. All living mounts within earshot of the character rear and bolt unless the players of their riders or team drivers makes a successful Charisma + Ride roll against a difficulty of the shouting Abyssal's Essence. Even if this roll succeeds, affected mounts remain skittish and add one to their Control Rating for the rest of the scene. This increase is cumulative if the Abyssal emits more than one such scream in a scene. Mount-Spooking Shout does not terrify the Abyssal's own steed, nor does the Charm have any effect on beasts other than pack animals or actual mounts.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Ride tree, pp. 218-219 (PDF 219-220).

name: Foundering Foal Gesture
summary: Gesturing sharply at a mount in her line of sight, the Abyssal curses her target with weakness and pain; the steed cannot move any faster than a walk unless pushed for short agonizing bursts by its rider.
requirements: Minimum Ride 4; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Mount-Spooking Shout.
mechanics: Gesturing sharply at a mount in her line of sight, the Abyssal curses her target with weakness and pain. The steed cannot move any faster than a walk unless pushed for short agonizing bursts by its rider. Foundering Foal Gesture can affect multiple animals at a cost of 4 motes each. As with Mount-Spooking Shout, this Charm only affects pack animals and steeds, although magical beasts and those strengthened with magic are also immune.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Ride tree, p. 219 (PDF 220). Closes out the Ride tree (7 Charms total).

name: Master Sailor's Memory
summary: Root of the Moonshadow Caste Sail tree; the character momentarily closes his eyes and dredges memories from the drowned dead of the Underworld, intuitively understanding the craft of sailing as if from decades of experience at sea.
requirements: Minimum Sail 2; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: The character momentarily closes his eyes and dredges memories from the drowned dead of the Underworld. When he opens his eyes, he intuitively understands the craft of sailing as though from decades of experience at sea.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Sail tree, root Charm, p. 219 (PDF 220).

name: Ghost on the Deck
summary: The Exalt adds one to his Sail rating for every mote spent, cannot raise a character's Sail above 5, and never botches balance rolls while using this Charm; the rest of the crew fly overboard from a hit but the deathknight stands unruffled.
requirements: Minimum Sail 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Master Sailor's Memory.
mechanics: The Exalt adds one dot to his Sail rating for every mote spent, although this Charm cannot raise a character's Sail above 5. In addition, Exalted using this Charm never botch a roll to keep their balance in tumultuous seas, but they can still fall normally. This Charm digs deeper into the memories of sailors long dead, allowing the character to guide his every movement. While this Charm is in effect, the character can perfectly balance and stride effortlessly across the deck or scurry up rigging without requiring a roll, even in the middle of a howling typhoon or on impact with a submerged reef. The rest of the crew may fly overboard from the impact or lashing waves, but the Exalt stands entirely unruffled. Characters using this Charm are also completely immune to seasickness.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Sail tree, p. 220 (PDF 221).

name: Crew Sustaining Technique
summary: Channeling the Essence of the Underworld and his own life force, the character can reduce a crew's need for food and rest; the character must spend one Willpower, plus 1 mote for every crewmember she wishes to enchant.
requirements: Minimum Sail 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Ghost on the Deck.
mechanics: Channeling the Essence of the Underworld and his own life force, the character may reduce a crew's need for food and rest. The character must spend one Willpower, plus 1 mote for every crewmember she wishes to enchant, thereafter the sailors' life energy is absorbed powering the Charm, reducing the cost to 1 mote per sailor per week. As a side effect, characters steadily kill off pests or vermin aboard the ship. If there are rats or other vermin aboard, their life energy is absorbed powering the Charm, reducing the cost to 1 mote per sailor per week. This side effect steadily kills off pests or vermin aboard the ship, and after two or three applications most sailors regard as a good omen. Unless a ship is very large or very infested, it takes only one or two applications of this Charm to completely eradicate all vermin aboard. A sailor enscorcelled with Crew Sustaining Technique needs about a quarter of the food, water and rest that he normally does. She does not suffer from scurvy or other dietary deficiencies from substandard rations and long unusually enervated. Long-term exposure is dangerous, however. If this Charm is used on a character for more days than her Stamina score, each successive day reduces her Stamina by one dot. Characters reduced to zero Stamina die at the rate of one point per day. Only after a character has fully recovered her Stamina can she be safely enchanted again. This Charm has no effect on beings whose statistics are otherwise superhuman.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Sail tree, p. 220 (PDF 221).

name: Phantom Sail Technique
summary: With this Charm, a character channels Essence to patch the rips and tears of a damaged sail; for the next 24 hours the sail behaves as if undamaged and provides appropriate propulsion.
requirements: Minimum Sail 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Master Sailor's Memory.
mechanics: With this Charm, a character channels Essence to patch the rips and tears of a damaged sail and rigging. The character concentrates and raises his hand, summoning a morass of shadows to spread over the targeted sail. For the next 24 hours, the sail behaves as if undamaged and provides appropriate propulsion. If a ship has multiple sails, the Exalt may have to use this Charm more than once. While Phantom Sail Technique can restore clinging tatters to full function, it cannot create a sail from nothing. At least some identifiable vestiges must remain.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Sail tree, p. 220 (PDF 221).

name: Ghost Wind Prana
summary: The Abyssal stands on deck, arms upraised and crackling with Essence as she summons a cold wind from the Underworld which exists to propel her vessel and displaces all natural breezes for that purpose.
requirements: Minimum Sail 5; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Phantom Sail Technique.
mechanics: The Abyssal stands on deck, arms upraised and crackling with Essence, as she summons a cold wind from the Underworld. This wind only exists to propel her vessel and displaces all natural breezes for that purpose, but otherwise, it does not disturb the water or wind for other vessels (though they may hear its eerie howling). Ships so enchanted move as though their sails were full in their rigging, regardless of the prevailing wind's direction or the course set by the helmsman. The spectral wind never gets deflected; ships sailing in a hurricane must still contend with the dangers of such a gale.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Sail tree, p. 220 (PDF 221).

name: Wind-Killing Stance
summary: With this Charm, an Abyssal can extend a zone of stillness from him, displacing even the fiercest gales with its periphery; the Exalt stands on deck and traces a horizontal arc, creating a sphere of calm.
requirements: Minimum Sail 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Ghost on the Deck, Ghost Wind Prana.
mechanics: With this Charm, an Abyssal can extend a zone of stillness from him, displacing even the fiercest gales with its periphery. The Exalt stands on deck and concentrates, tracing a horizontal arc with his arms. At the conclusion of the gesture, a spherical wave of Essence flashes out to the arc to a radius of (the character's permanent Essence x 15) yards. This artificial stillness moves with the Exalt and lasts for one scene or until his creator dies or moves more than a yard from his original location on deck. The character can still speak and gesture normally while maintaining Wind-Killing Stance, however. Wind-Killing Stance cannot stop magical storms or breezes created by magical beings unless the deathknight's Essence substantially less powerful (Storyteller's discretion). This Charm is primarily to weather storms and to prevent enemy sailing vessels from escaping.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Sail tree, pp. 220-221 (PDF 221-222).

name: Hull-Hardening Technique
summary: By laying hands against a hull and willing Essence to flow through its timbers, an Abyssal with this Charm can mystically reinforce her vessel; the ship gains 1L of soak per mote spent, purchasable multiple times.
requirements: Minimum Sail 5; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Ghost Wind Prana.
mechanics: By laying hands against a hull and willing Essence to flow through its timbers, an Abyssal with this Charm can mystically reinforce her vessel. The ship gains 1L of soak per mote spent, although the deathknight cannot purchase more points of soak than her Stamina + Sail. This limit applies to all applications of the Charm in a scene. Hull-Hardening Technique does not require Willpower if used for another application while the Charm remains active. Hulls regularly treated with this Charm look bleached and weathered before their time, although they retain the durability of their true age.
cost: 1 mote per L of soak, plus 1 Willpower
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Sail tree, pp. 220-221 (PDF 221-222).

name: Hull-Restoring Meditation
summary: The Abyssal extends his anima through the hull, caulking and patching breaches and split seams with raw Essence; the amount of Essence spent to repair damage scales with the ship's damage and size.
requirements: Minimum Sail 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Hull-Hardening Technique.
mechanics: The Abyssal extends his anima through the hull, caulking and patching breaches and split seams with raw Essence. This energy calcifies into a durable material with the consistency and appearance of bleached bone. Repairing combat damage requires the Abyssal to spend motes equal to the ship's destroyed or damaged rating, as appropriate to the severity of the damage. For non-combat repairs and general caulking, the Storyteller should assign an Essence cost based on the severity of the damage and the ship's size. Sealing a leaky warship requires considerably more Essence than a river yacht. While this Charm can stave off certain destruction by sealing massive breaches, it does not remove handling penalties for water trapped in the hull. Such penalties remain until the water is pumped or bailed out normally.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Sail tree, p. 221 (PDF 222).

name: Unsinkable Derelict Preservation
summary: Although it is possible to strengthen and repair ships with lesser Charms, an Abyssal with Unsinkable Derelict Preservation can enchant a ship to ignore damage entirely for one day, keeping out water and moving with its normal maneuverability and speed.
requirements: Minimum Sail 5; Minimum Essence 4; Prerequisite Charms: Hull-Restoring Meditation.
mechanics: Although it is possible to strengthen and repair ships with lesser Charms, an Abyssal with Unsinkable Derelict Preservation can enchant a ship to ignore damage entirely. The Exalt channels Essence through the ship's hull, temporarily sealing all breaks and gashes with translucent wisps of relic from the Underworld. Ships enscorcelled with this Charm act entirely as if whole, keeping out water and moving with their normal maneuverability and speed.
