Further damage is also similarly ignored for the Charm's duration. Once the Charm's protection ends, severely damaged vessels take on water and sink normally. This Charm can even restore a rotting hulk to full operation, so long as enough of the ship's remains identify the ship. Vessels that have broken asunder cannot be enchanted; they lack the material foundation to accept relic grafts. Ultimately, the Storyteller is the final arbiter of whether or not a ship retains enough substance to preserve. This Charm can affect First Age designs.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Sail tree, p. 221 (PDF 222). Closes out the Sail tree (9 Charms total).

name: Exquisite Etiquette Style
summary: Root of the Moonshadow Caste Socialize tree; the Abyssal attunes his mind to the communal memories of the dead to act with faultless (if not officious) propriety and decorum.
requirements: Minimum Socialize 2; Minimum Essence 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: The Abyssal attunes his mind to the communal memories of the dead to act with faultless propriety and decorum. Characters under the effects of this Charm become faultlessly -- but not officiously -- polite. They instinctively know the appropriate greeting customs or table manners for their situation and never run the risk of making an unintentional faux pas. This Charm is paramount importance when dealing with ancient ghosts whose cultures and customs have long since fallen to the passing of Ages.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Socialize tree, root Charm, p. 221 (PDF 222).

name: Imprecation of Ill Manners
summary: The Abyssal concentrates on a victim in his line of sight, silently projecting a surge of visceral anger into her subconscious; for the rest of the turn, the target loses one die from all Socialize dice pools for every mote spent.
requirements: Minimum Socialize 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Exquisite Etiquette Style.
mechanics: The Abyssal concentrates on a victim in his line of sight, silently projecting a surge of visceral anger into her subconscious. For the rest of the turn, the target loses one die from all Socialize dice pools for every mote spent. This reduction manifests as poor manners, Freudian slips and other, similar gaffes. It is impossible to determine that the Charm's target is acting under the influence of a curse or similar magical means, although astute observers (Perception + Awareness 4+) may suspect that something is amiss.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Socialize tree, p. 222 (PDF 223).

name: Loyalty Withering Technique
summary: Caressing a victim's mind with the corrupting taint of the Void, an Abyssal with this Charm can plant seeds of doubt in the faithful and erode trust in favor of treachery, temporarily eroding a Virtue by a number of successes.
requirements: Minimum Socialize 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Exquisite Etiquette Style.
mechanics: Caressing a victim's mind with the corrupting taint of the Void, an Abyssal with this Charm can plant seeds of doubt in the faithful and erode trust in favor of treachery. The character need only spend a few minutes talking to her target; her player then rolls Manipulation + Socialize against a difficulty chosen by the Storyteller. This difficulty reflects the overall devotion of the target to the selected individual or cause. If she rolls enough successes, the target becomes suspicious and hostile toward whomever or whatever the Abyssal desires. This treacherous dislike lasts a number of hours equal to the deathknight's permanent Essence. If the Exalt receives more successes than necessary, this duration is measured in days rather than hours. This Charm has no effect on beings with a higher Essence rating than the Abyssal.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Socialize tree, p. 222 (PDF 223).

name: Heart-Hardening Method
summary: By infecting a target's very soul with festering Essence, the Abyssal can sow doubt in the importance of a particular Virtue, temporarily or permanently reducing a rating via a Manipulation + Socialize roll.
requirements: Minimum Socialize 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Loyalty Withering Technique.
mechanics: By infecting a target's very soul with festering Essence, the Abyssal can sow doubt on the importance of a particular Virtue, casting doubt on the target. The Exalt must spend several minutes talking to the target, casting doubt on the importance of a particular Virtue; her player then rolls Manipulation + Socialize, with a difficulty equal to the targeted Virtue. The victim temporarily loses one dot of the appropriate Virtue for every success in excess of its rating. If the number of successes exceed the target's Willpower score, the target also loses a permanent dot of the Virtue. Whether temporary or permanent, this Charm cannot reduce a Virtue below a rating of one. Virtues that are temporarily diminished return at the rate of one dot per hour. The Abyssal can even use this Charm on herself, with appropriate successes detracting from the targeted Virtue as normal. While this rationalization process has its uses -- particularly in situations when scruples are a liability -- the Abyssal risks permanent Virtue loss if she rationalizes too well. Although a victim ensorcelled by this Charm retains his Nature, his behavior reflects his new Virtue rating. A Thrillseeker deprived of his once-considerable Valor will be torn by desires and a curiosity he can no longer bring himself to express. Likewise, a Survivor dropped to Compassion 1 will do practically anything to anyone in order to preserve his existence.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Socialize tree, p. 222 (PDF 223).

name: Sin-Sensing Meditation
summary: As cynical as they are pragmatic, characters with this Charm recognize that everyone can be bought; their price might be jade or jewels, a secret vice instead -- but regardless, there is always something a person cannot resist or refuse.
requirements: Minimum Socialize 5; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Heart-Hardening Method.
mechanics: As cynical as they are pragmatic, characters with this Charm recognize that everyone can be bought. Their price might be jade or jewels, a secret vice instead -- but regardless, there is always something a person cannot resist or refuse. To have the object of her desire, an Abyssal knows precisely what that object is for her target. He may not have the means of satisfying the desire in question, particularly if it is nigh impossible to acquire, but at least, he knows. The Storyteller should consider the nature of a target's weakness, keeping in mind the target's Nature and Temperance score. Low Temperance characters are less disciplined and, thus, have easier wants to satisfy. High Temperance characters are invariably more difficult and complicated to satiate. It is always possible that some beatific saint exists on whom this Charm would have no effect, but no deathknight has ever met such a person in the decadent Age of Sorrows.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Socialize tree, p. 222 (PDF 223).

name: Passion-Unveiling Glance
summary: With this Charm, an Abyssal perceives the flickering aura of emotion and passion overlaying her target, gleaning the target's most surface feelings or, with more successes, a full sense of currently felt emotions and Virtue/Willpower allocation.
requirements: Minimum Socialize 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: With this Charm, an Abyssal perceives the flickering aura of emotion and passion overlaying her target. The Abyssal's player rolls Perception + Socialize against standard difficulty if the target is not trying to conceal or misrepresent his feelings. Otherwise, the target's player reflexively rolls Manipulation + Performance to resist. The amount of information the Abyssal gleans depends on the number of successes rolled beyond what the target may have garnered. Simple success reveals the target's most surface feelings, and gauge their rough proportion to one another (i.e., strong admiration with a touch of jealousy). Five or more successes allow the Abyssal to sense all emotions her target currently feels, as well as give her a rough sense of the target's permanent Willpower and Virtue allocation (weak, unremarkable, strong, overpowering, etc.). Regardless of the successes rolled, this Charm does not provide context. Even if a deathknight notices coiling tendrils of hatred in a target's aura, she doesn't automatically know who she hates or why he hates.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Socialize tree, p. 223 (PDF 224).

name: Intimations of Mortality
summary: Some Abyssal Exalted are particularly adept at seeding the minds of mortals with doubts about the true nature of life and death that they come to be obsessed with their own mortality, becoming depressed and withdrawn if the roll succeeds.
requirements: Minimum Socialize 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Passion-Unveiling Glance.
mechanics: Some Abyssal Exalted are particularly adept at seeding the minds of mortals with such doubts about the true nature of life and death that they come to be obsessed with their own mortality. A deathknight must speak with a target at least briefly (the exchange need only be a few sentences), and the Abyssal's player then makes a Manipulation + Socialize roll with a difficulty of the target's permanent Essence. If successful, the target becomes depressed and withdrawn, suffering a +2 difficulty to all Social rolls for the next 24 hours. If this Charm is used continuously on an unExalted target for more than days than her Conviction rating, her depression blossoms into an actual derangement. Targets afflicted this way continue to suffer Social penalties even after the Charm wears off.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Moonshadow Caste Socialize tree, p. 223 (PDF 224). Closes out the Socialize tree (7 Charms) and, with it, all five Moonshadow Caste Charm trees (Bureaucracy, Linguistics, Ride, Sail, Socialize).

name: Necromancy Framework and Circles
summary: Chapter Six's necromancy system: three ascending circles of death magic (Shadowlands, Labyrinth, Void) mirroring Terrestrial/Celestial/Solar Circle Sorcery, requiring an appropriate prerequisite Charm per circle and concurrent Charm-plus-spell invocation; botched necromancy inflicts aggravated Essence damage.
requirements: Chapter Six framework overview; not itself a selectable power.
mechanics: Necromancy channels the dead Essence of the Underworld rather than the living Essence of Creation, but this distinction does not make necromancy inherently evil, any more than sorcery is inherently good. Sorcerers and necromancers alike can perform beneficial or malevolent works; the intention and action of each magician is what matters. Necromancy is divided into three circles of power with separate spells at each level. Instead of ascending from earth to Heaven as with Terrestrial, Celestial, and Solar Circle Sorcery, necromancy's three circles descend in growing power from Shadowlands to Labyrinth and, finally, to Void. Characters using necromancy must possess the appropriate Charm to do so and must invoke both spell and Charm concurrently to work an effect. Minimum casting times for each spell match those of parallel sorcery circles, as does the time and effort required to learn or invent new spells. One notable difference is the danger of miscast necromancy versus sorcery: necromancy channels the raw energy of Oblivion, so Essence burns from a botched spell inflict aggravated damage. Precious few necromancers survive their first serious mistake. Though the Abyssal are the undisputed masters of necromancy, they are not the only Exalted to practice death magic; any Celestial Exalted can learn ShadowlandsCircle Necromancy (substituting Intelligence for Occult in the Lunar variation), and Solar Exalted can learn as deep as the Labyrinth Circle, though the only non-Abyssal necromancers in the Age of Sorrows are a tiny handful of the Favored of Saturn. Twilight Caste sorcerers were the original necromancers of the First Age.
notes: Chapter Six: Necromancy, framework/rules overview, pp. 222-224 (PDF 223-225). The specific 'appropriate Charm' gating each circle (paralleling Terrestrial/Celestial/Solar Circle Sorcery) was not located as its own stat block in the rendered Chapter Five or Chapter Six pages; flagged in the family source-manifest rulesNotes for follow-up. This row captures the framework text itself rather than a selectable power, matching the reference-only disposition used for equivalent Sidereal astrology/Charm-framework rows.

name: Hungry Creeping Shadow
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; the necromancer opens her mouth as if to scream, gathering into a viscous black ooze pours forth, forming a horrible amorphous creature of liquid shadow that pursues any one target in her creator's line of sight.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The necromancer opens her mouth as if to scream, gathering into a viscous black ooze pours forth, forming a horrible amorphous creature of liquid shadow that pursues any one target in her creator's line of sight. The beast has Physical Attributes and a Brawl Ability equal to its creator's permanent Essence and a number of health levels equal to its creator's Stamina + Essence. It is immune to all purely kinetic damage, such as from swords or fists, but has no soak against fire or magical damage. Like the undead, it lacks Virtues but never fails Valor checks. The Hungry Creeping Shadow can flow up walls and through narrow pipes or under most doors and unerringly follows its quarry. Once it catches its victim, the creature will attempt to clench and slowly crush the life from her. Upon its demise, it boils away to a slimy residue.
notes: Chapter Six: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 224 (PDF 225).

name: Iron Countermagic
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; with this spell, the Exalt can absorb and smother the energy of hostile necromancy, or alternately extinguish a single Shadowlands Circle spell directed at her, and can counter higher-circle spells at greater mote costs.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: With this spell, the Exalt can absorb and smother the energy of hostile necromancy. If the character spends 10 motes, she may slash at the air, tearing ribbons of black power to swirl and bleed around her person. This shield negates all hostile spells of the Shadowlands Circle directed at her until the end of the next turn, but its cold seeps into her joints and bones, inflicting a -2 penalty to all Physical actions for as long as it persists. Alternately, for 20 motes, the caster can extinguish a single Shadowlands Circle spell within a number of feet equaling her permanent Essence x 50. Excalted opponents, but they are always extras in the process of being cast are torn asunder. This spell is extremely fast and takes effect as soon as the character spends Willpower. Countermagic can break bonds of servitude wrought by necromancy. Also, spells countered by Iron Countermagic shatter without inflicting any side effects; if used to counter a lower circle, the countermagic entirely annihilates the spell with no side effects or collateral damage. Counterered Void Circle spells still mar bystanders and ravage the earth, although in most cases, the backlash pale compared to the intended effects. More powerful versions of this spell exist higher on either circle: Onyx for Labyrinth and Void, Obsidian for Void. Each protects against spells of their circle or below. If used to counter a lower circle, the countermagic utterly annihilates the spell with no side effects or collateral damage. Necromantic countermagic can also oppose sorcery if it is one circle or higher, vice versa. Thus, Sapphire Countermagic (see Exalted, p. 221) may counter Shadowlands Circle spells as well, and Obsidian Countermagic may block Celestial Circle Sorcery, etc. The personal shield/direct extinguishing costs for Onyx and Obsidian are 15 motes/20 motes and 20 motes/25 motes respectively.
notes: Chapter Six: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, pp. 224-225 (PDF 225-226). OCR of this spell's rules text is degraded in places (garbled clauses around the counter-lower-circle wording); the core mechanic (personal shield vs. targeted dispel, higher-circle Onyx/Obsidian variants) is clear, but flagged as unreviewed pending a cleaner re-read.

name: Piercing the Shroud
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; the necromancer concentrates and murmurs a discordant incantation that shakes the earth in the immediate vicinity and unnerves all natural animals who hear it, opening a shimmering rift into the Labyrinth.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The necromancer concentrates and murmurs a discordant incantation that shakes the earth in the immediate vicinity and unnerves all natural animals who hear it. This chant takes 10 minutes to complete, casting no penalty. At the conclusion of the chant, the Exalt reaches out with her hand and cuts a vertical slash in the fabric of Creation as the blade passes, this rift opens a shimmering rift for a number of turns equal to her creator's permanent Essence before closing with a horrible sucking sound. This spell only permits a necromancer to enter the Labyrinth -- the character must find her own way out.
notes: Chapter Six: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 225 (PDF 226).

name: Raise the Skeletal Horde
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; as she prepares this spell, a ball of crackling Essence grows and envelops the necromancer's clenched hand, erupting at the conclusion into a cascade of jagged lightning that strikes the nearest interred corpses within 100 yards, raising them as common zombies or skeletons.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: As she prepares this spell, a ball of crackling Essence grows and envelops the necromancer's clenched hand. The sphere glows darkly and pulsates before, at the conclusion of the spell, erupting in a cascade of jagged lightning that arcs and forks to strike the nearest interred human carcasses or skeletons within 100 yards. Corpses struck by this energy spend the rest of the turn getting their feet or clawing their way free from the earth as appropriate to their location. Skeletons and zombies raised with this spell have the same statistics as common zombies (see Exalted p. 299), although they are always extras. Once raised, such creatures obey their creator to the best of their limited Intelligence. This spell creates one zombie for every 5 motes spent. Alternately, the necromancer may opt to spend only 3 motes per zombie, but creatures lose all animation at the end of the scene. Characters may not create both permanent and temporary minions the same casting.
notes: Chapter Six: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 225 (PDF 226). Its own entry is immediately followed on the same page by two named Labyrinth Circle variants, Arisen Legion and Call the Greater Servitor (see those rows), presented as modified versions of this spell rather than fully independent write-ups.

name: Arisen Legion
summary: Labyrinth Circle variant of Raise the Skeletal Horde; duplicates that spell's effect but reduces the Essence cost to 3 motes per permanent zombie or 1 mote per temporary zombie.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: Arisen Legion duplicates the effect of Raise the Skeletal Horde but reduces the Essence cost to 3 motes for a permanent zombie or 1 mote for a temporary zombie.
cost: 3 motes per permanent zombie or 1 mote per temporary zombie
notes: Chapter Six: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 225 (PDF 226). Presented in the source as a named Labyrinth Circle variant appended directly to the Raise the Skeletal Horde entry rather than as a separately headed spell block; given its own row here per this pass's 'every spell gets its own row' scope.

name: Call the Greater Servitor
summary: Labyrinth Circle variant of Raise the Skeletal Horde; costs 6 motes per minion, cannot create temporary zombies or more corpses in a single casting than the necromancer's Occult score, but its zombies are never extras and have Intelligence and Melee 2, letting them use weapons, wear armor, and follow more complex instructions.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The second variant, Call the Greater Servitor, costs 6 motes for each minion, but the character cannot create temporary zombies or raise more corpses in a single casting than his Occult score. Zombies raised with Call the Greater Servitor are never extras and have an Intelligence and Melee of 2, allowing them to use weapons or wear armor and to follow more complicated instructions.
notes: Chapter Six: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 225 (PDF 226). Presented in the source as a named Labyrinth Circle variant appended directly to the Raise the Skeletal Horde entry rather than as a separately headed spell block; given its own row here per this pass's 'every spell gets its own row' scope.

name: Rune of Sweet Passing
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; the necromancer spends an hour painting an elaborate pattern of glyphs on a naked mortal's skin using paint made from human blood mixed with soil taken from a grave, cursing the target to become a ghost upon death.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The necromancer spends an hour painting an elaborate pattern of glyphs on a naked mortal's skin. The Exalt must paint using paint made from human blood mixed with soil taken from a grave. At the conclusion of the ritual, the runes flare with red light and soak into the target's skin. Once a mortal has been branded with this rune, she is assured of becoming a ghost upon death, although she does not know when the target dies, although he does not know the circumstances or location of her passing. This spell creates ghosts; it does not compel their service or loyalty. Targets of this spell need not be willing, although unwilling targets must generally be restrained. This spell has no effect on the Exalted or other magical beings.
notes: Chapter Six: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 225 (PDF 226).

name: Shade Prison Amulet
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; this spell can enchant any piece of bone jewelry to become a vessel for hungry ghosts; the amulet touches any one hungry ghost, sucking the soul into itself in a swirl of wind and imprisoning it so long as the talisman remains intact.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: This spell can enchant any piece of bone jewelry to become a vessel for hungry ghosts. The necromancer etches runes onto the object's surface and invests it with Essence. This amulet touches any one hungry ghost, it sucks the soul into itself in a swirl of wind. This amulet's imprisonment lasts only so long as the talisman remains intact. Once the prison breaks, the ghost escapes to wreak havoc, although it will not attack the person who freed it. Breaking a prison by daylight destroys the trapped spirit. A Labyrinth Circle version of this spell, Bauble of the Captive Soul, follows the same rules as this spell but can capture any ghost it touches. This spell costs 15 motes.
notes: Chapter Six: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 225 (PDF 226). Cross-references a Labyrinth Circle upgrade ('Bauble of the Captive Soul') not yet catalogued (Labyrinth Circle spells remain out of scope for this round).

name: Soul Brand
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; by pressing her palm against an unExalted mortal's flesh and whispering a benediction to the Malfeans, a necromancer with this spell can mystically tattoo him with a rune of power that confers the same protection as a Ghost-Warding Glyph.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: By pressing her palm against an unExalted mortal's flesh and whispering a benediction to the Malfeans, a necromancer with this spell can mystically tattoo him with a rune of power. This rune confers the same protection as a Ghost-Warding Glyph (see page 216), but the effects persist unless the necromancer removes them. If the glyph is removed, whether through countermagic or by the whim of its creator, it inflicts the necromancer's permanent Essence in aggravated damage as it burns away. Should a mortal ever Exalt, his rune vanishes without a trace, causing no injury. This spell is otherwise used to brand the foreheads or palms of favored servants.
notes: Chapter Six: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, pp. 225-226 (PDF 226-227).

name: Summon Ghost
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; this spell calls one of the Restless Dead and binds him to the service of the necromancer, requiring an unbroken circle of blood or bone-dust cast at night and an Essence contest to compel service.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: This spell calls one of the Restless Dead and binds him to the service of the necromancer. This spell can only be cast at night and involves an hour-long ritual requiring an unbroken circle of blood or bone-dust. The character must also know the name of the ghost he wishes to summon or have a piece of her corpse in his possession. The ghost's overwrought soul must overpower the necromancer's willpower or Essence contest, costing the target's Willpower + Essence test. For every 5 additional motes the Exalt spends casting, the ghost's pool decreases by one, until one side accumulates three more successes than the other. If the ghost wins, he immediately escapes the portal and cannot be recalled for a full year. If the Exalt wins, the ghost must obey her for one year or fulfill a single task that can have infinite duration. This binding only forces the ghost to obey the letter of the necromancer's command, rather than her actual intent, but most ghosts will comply rather than risk the wrath of an Exalted. Once the ghost fulfills its obligation, it vanishes back to its original location in the Underworld. Although ghosts make excellent servants, their usefulness in the living world is limited by their difficulty in regaining Essence. Necromancers employing such vassals must be sure to feed them motes of Essence, either from their own or from libations of human blood. Though ghosts resent servitude, if only out of fear. On the other hand, summoning a courtier or honored servant of a Deathlord can have dire repercussions instead.
notes: Chapter Six: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 226 (PDF 227).

name: Walking War Machine
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; few weapons sow as much terror among living armies as the undead siege engines employed by the Deathlords; with this spell, a necromancer can animate such devices, first building or overseeing the building of the machine.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: Few weapons sow as much terror among living armies as the undead siege engines employed by the Deathlords. With this spell, a necromancer can use Essence to animate such devices. The Exalt must first build or oversee the building of the monstrosity, with his player making an extended Intelligence + Craft (Necrosurgery) roll to represent this task. Grafts and other pieces cut and stitched together and any grafts of metal inserted where appropriate. For a spine chain needs one success for every stage of complexity it needs. Once the creature is complete, the character simply touches it and invests 5 motes for every success needed to assemble it. Monsters created with this Charm serve their master to the best of his limited Intelligence. Statistics for spine chains can be found on page 300 of Exalted. Other devices are left for players' imagination and Storyteller approval but should be of a similar power level.
notes: Chapter Six: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, pp. 226-227 (PDF 227-228). Closes out the Shadowlands (First) Circle spell list (9 spells).

name: Exquisite Undead Aide
summary: Labyrinth Circle spell; instead of raising a mindless shambling horde, a necromancer with this spell can create a single powerful zombie servant to act as a lieutenant or majordomo, one who never decays further and can speak in clipped rasping phrases.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: Instead of raising a mindless shambling horde, a necromancer with this spell can create a single powerful servant to act as a lieutenant or majordomo. The creature begins with the same statistics as a zombie (see Exalted p. 299), with the following modifications: all Attributes have a minimum rating of 2, the creature gains an Appearance of dots equal to its creator's Intelligence + Occult, and it knows all Abilities, though none can exceed the necromancer's own rating. The creature never decays any further, although it exudes a distinctive musty reek that clearly marks it as one of the undead. The creature may speak in clipped, rasping phrases, although it only speaks in response to questions from its master or in fulfillment of her orders. It is not considered an extra and has a full complement of health levels.
notes: Chapter Six: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 226 (PDF 227). Opens the Labyrinth (Second) Circle spell list, immediately following the 'The Labyrinth Circle' section-intro prose on the same page.

name: Hundred Shade Breath
summary: Labyrinth Circle spell; the necromancer exhales a glowing blue fog of curling tendrils that coalesce into a swarm of hungry ghosts, one for every 2 motes of Essence spent, though the spell is useless by day since sunlight would burn the horde to ash.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The necromancer inhales and concentrates, building the spell inside her lungs. When the magic is ready, she opens her mouth and a glowing blue fog rushes out in dozens of curling tendrils as she exhales. Over the next turn, these wisps coalesce into hungry ghosts -- one for every 2 motes of Essence spent. These ghosts have normal statistics (see Exalted p. 300) and are all extras. Obviously, this spell is of no use during the day, as sunlight would instantly burn the assembled horde to ash. At the end of the scene in which they were summoned, any 'surviving' ghosts dissolve to mist and flow back into the necromancer's mouth. Motes spent on this spell remain committed so long as the ghosts remain, but the character frees 2 motes from the committed total every time one perishes.
notes: Chapter Six: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, pp. 226-227 (PDF 227-228).

name: Ivory Razor Forest
summary: Labyrinth Circle spell; the necromancer gestures toward her enemies and an invisible shockwave skims the earth, causing dozens or hundreds of razor-edged bone spines to tear up from the ground at great speed, inflicting 8L damage to anything in their path.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The necromancer gestures in the direction of her enemies, and a shockwave of Essence skims the earth toward them. The wave is invisible and causes no injury. However, in its wake, dozens or even hundreds of great spines of gleaming bone tear up through the earth at great speed, to a maximum height of the caster's permanent Essence in yards. The razor-edged blades cut through everything in their path, inflicting 8L damage to anything that cannot be blocked, only dodged. The spikes affect a total area of (the necromancer's Charisma + Occult x 10) square yards, although this area can be divided into any shape or configuration as the caster sees fit. Some prefer to break apart troop formations while others grow the bones into impassable fences or ramparts. The blades shatter into dust after a number of days equal to their creator's Essence, but have the durability of a brick wall until that time (see Exalted, p. 239). The blades are densely packed enough that nothing larger than a rabbit can slip through the cracks, and being thrown against them also inflicts 8L.
notes: Chapter Six: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 227 (PDF 228).

name: Reaping the Fallen
summary: Labyrinth Circle spell; the necromancer opens her anima to draw power from death, gaining 1 mote for every sentient being that dies within a league of her, up to her usual maximum, making it most useful during mass carnage such as a massacre or military battle.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: With this spell, a necromancer opens her soul to draw power from death. Her anima erupts to its full iconic glory regardless of whether she spent Personal or Peripheral Essence, while her face contorts into a mask of inhuman rage and hunger. For the rest of the scene, the character gains 1 mote for every sentient being dying within a league of her, up to her usual maximum. Obviously, this spell is only useful in the presence of mass carnage, such as a massacre or a military battle. In such settings, the Storyteller should assign how many motes the character gains each turn instead of awarding Essence on a per death basis.
notes: Chapter Six: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 227 (PDF 228). Immediately followed in the source by a named Void Circle variant, Blood from the Slaughter (see that row).

name: Blood from the Slaughter
summary: Void Circle variant of Reaping the Fallen; instead of gaining Essence, the necromancer regenerates one level of bashing or lethal damage for every sentient being killed within a league each turn, though never more levels per turn than her permanent Essence.
requirements: Necromancy: Void Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: A Void Circle version of this spell, Blood from the Slaughter, instead allows the necromancer to supplant her own life force with the energy released by carnage. At the end of each turn, the character regenerates one level of bashing or lethal damage for every living sentient killed within one league, but the character cannot regenerate more levels per turn than her permanent Essence.
notes: Chapter Six: Necromancy, The Void Circle, p. 227 (PDF 228). Presented in the source as a named Void Circle variant appended directly to the Reaping the Fallen entry rather than as a separately headed spell block; given its own row here per this pass's 'every spell gets its own row' scope. First Void Circle spell to appear in the book, though it precedes the formal 'THE VOID CIRCLE' section heading that opens with Abyssal Aegis.

name: Spiteful Passing
summary: Labyrinth Circle spell; facing the bitterness of his own demise, a necromancer with this spell unleashes his hate in a final blast of power as he dies, dealing lethal damage to all living beings and Fair Folk in range and bypassing armor.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: Faced with the bitterness of his own demise, a necromancer with this spell may unleash his hate in a final blast of power. Although he must still spend a turn concentrating, the character need only speak one word to cast this spell. He may scream in defiance or weakly cough his last syllable from blood-flecked lips, but the effects remain the same. His body arches in pain and expires as searing light erupts from his opened mouth, eyes, and wounds. All living beings and Fair Folk within a number of yards equal to the necromancer's permanent Essence suffer his permanent Essence in dice of lethal damage, plus one additional die for every point remaining in his pool. This damage bypasses armor. It is soaked only with the victim's own natural soak, and it inflicts no physical trauma -- victims killed by the spell simply drop where they stand, and survivors feel a terrible cold grip them. All plants in range wither and die. The necromancer's corpse rots to dust within moments of the blast.
notes: Chapter Six: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, pp. 227-228 (PDF 228-229). This spell can only be cast at the moment of the necromancer's own death; the source text does not give a mote cost since it consumes the caster's remaining Essence pool as its cost basis, hence 'Special'.

name: Stealing the Gathered Breath
summary: Labyrinth Circle spell; the necromancer opens her mouth and inhales, drawing Essence from every living being within her permanent Essence x 5 yards, soaked only with Stamina, restoring 1 mote to the necromancer per level of damage inflicted and visible to onlookers as pale light rushing into her maw.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The necromancer opens her mouth and inhales, drawing energy from every sentient living being within the character's permanent Essence x 5 yards. All victims within range suffer one die of lethal damage, soaked only with Stamina. Each level of damage actually inflicted by this spell restores 1 mote of Essence to the necromancer. Energy harvested with this spell can be seen by all onlookers as streams of pale light rushing from the victims to the necromancer's maw.
notes: Chapter Six: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 228 (PDF 229).

name: Striking Spectre Lash
summary: Labyrinth Circle spell; a long tendril of solidified darkness grows from the necromancer's wrist or palm, striking like a dart or octopus tentacle and inflicting normal or crippling grappling attacks; motes spent before an attack roll add automatic successes to hit or Essence damage.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: Upon casting this spell, a long tendril of solidified darkness grows from the necromancer's wrist or palm. This serpentine appendage undulates and coils of its own volition, striking more like a darting snake or an octopus tentacle than any mundane whip. The lash has a Speed, Accuracy, and Defense rating equal to its master's Essence and a score and a length in yards of five times this value. Its base damage equals its creator's Strength + Essence. In addition to inflicting normal damage and permitting grappling attacks, the whip can kill unwary mortals and animals outright. If the necromancer reflexively spends 2 motes before making his attack roll and successfully hits, the victim's player must make a reflexive Essence roll. If this roll fails, the victim falls dead with a look of horror frozen in her face. Exalts, spirits, Fair Folk, and other magical beings are notably larger than humans are immune to this effect so long as their Stamina exceeds the necromancer's Essence rating.
notes: Chapter Six: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 228 (PDF 229). Closes out the Labyrinth (Second) Circle spell list (9 spells: Exquisite Undead Aide, Hundred Shade Breath, Arisen Legion, Call the Greater Servitor, Ivory Razor Forest, Reaping the Fallen, Spiteful Passing, Stealing the Gathered Breath, Striking Spectre Lash).

name: The Void Circle
summary: Section-intro prose opening the Void (Third) Circle of necromancy: though it is generally believed that no Exalted apart from the Abyssals can practice necromancy at this level, Solar Exalted once probed the powers of the Labyrinth Circle and could do so again with the proper tutelage, but none save the deathknights and their Deathlord masters can invoke magic of the Void itself.
requirements: Chapter Six framework overview; not itself a selectable power.
mechanics: Though it is generally believed by savants that no Exalted apart from the Abyssals can practice the discipline of necromancy, such is not the case. Solar Exalted once probed the powers of the Labyrinth Circle and could do so again with the proper tutelage. Still, none save the deathknights and their Deathlord masters can invoke magic of the Void itself. Indeed, no scholar of the First Age ever suspected such terrible magic was possible. Yet, it is with magic of this circle that the Deathlords created and unleashed the Great Contagion, and it is with this circle that the sorcerer-kings of the Underworld now seduce and corrupt nascent Solar Exalted to the service of Oblivion.
notes: Chapter Six: Necromancy, section-intro prose for The Void Circle, p. 228 (PDF 229), immediately preceding Abyssal Aegis. Note that Blood from the Slaughter (a Void Circle spell) is presented earlier on the page as a variant of the Labyrinth Circle's Reaping the Fallen, ahead of this formal section heading; see that row.

name: Abyssal Aegis
summary: Void Circle spell; until the next sunrise, the necromancer gains extra bashing and lethal soak against all magic specifically designed to cause extra damage or trauma to Abyssal Exalted, Deathlords, or denizens of the Underworld, though it does not make the Exalt immune to an attack simply because it was augmented with such damage.
requirements: Necromancy: Void Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: Until the next sunrise, the necromancer gains extra bashing and lethal soak equal to his permanent Essence. In addition, the character is completely immune to all magic specifically designed to cause extra damage or trauma to Abyssal Exalted, Deathlords, or denizens of the Underworld. This protection does not make the Exalt immune to an attack augmented with such magic, although the extra effect is negated. Thus, blasts from the Zenith Caste anima power vanish in a swirl of shadow before they touch the necromancer, but Blazing Solar Bolt still hits, albeit for lethal damage only.
notes: Chapter Six: Necromancy, The Void Circle, p. 228 (PDF 229). Opens the formal 'THE VOID CIRCLE' section (Blood from the Slaughter, catalogued earlier as a Reaping the Fallen variant, is chronologically the first Void Circle spell to appear on the page but precedes this section heading).

name: Anguished Shade Harvest
summary: Void Circle spell; this potent spell consecrates a stretch of land so that all who suffer violent death within its borders become hungry ghosts, requiring the necromancer to journey there physically as quickly as possible, pacing the intended boundary of the effect.
requirements: Necromancy: Void Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: This potent spell consecrates a stretch of land so that all who suffer violent death within its borders become hungry ghosts. The necromancer must begin this spell as the sun dips beneath the horizon and spend the required Essence. He then journeys as quickly as possible, physically pacing the intended boundary of the effect. He cannot fly or transport himself magically, although he may use a mount to aid his travel. If he keeps moving without reversing his path and arrives at his original location before midnight, the spell takes effect. Malignant black clouds grow in the sky to cover the entire area, casting the earth into murky gloom even after daybreak. Any mortal who suffers a violent or painful demise in the afflicted area before the last rays of sunlight leave the sky arises as a hungry ghost when the last rays of sunlight leave the sky. These ghosts will not attack the necromancer, but they are not under his control in any way. Hungry ghosts created with this spell have normal statistics (see Exalted, p. 301) but are always considered extras.
notes: Chapter Six: Necromancy, The Void Circle, p. 228 (PDF 229). The source text's middle sentences describing the sunset/sunlight timing read as slightly redundant/looping in the render ('before the last rays of sunlight leave the sky arises... when the last rays of sunlight leave the sky'); flagged for re-verification against a cleaner render, though the overall mechanic (violent deaths in the consecrated area become hungry ghosts at nightfall) is clear.

name: Blood Monsoon
summary: Void Circle spell; the necromancer cuts her palm and flings a spray of blood into the air, forming a mile-wide disk-shaped cloud that eventually covers a radius in miles equal to her permanent Essence, after which a torrential downpour of blood drenches the earth below, harming plants, animals, and unprotected humans and attracting hungry ghosts.
requirements: Necromancy: Void Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The necromancer cuts her palm and flings a spray of blood into the air. Instead, these droplets never fall to the earth. Instead, the rise and multiply until a column of bedded crimson ascends in an obscene geyser into the sky. This pillar reaches a height of one mile, it blossoms outward, growing into a disk-shaped cloud that eventually covers a radius in miles equal to its creator's permanent Essence. This entire process takes one hour. Although the necromancer can take other actions during this time, the Essence powering the spell remains committed until it completely runs its course. After the cloud reaches its full size, a torrential downpour of blood drenches the earth below in gore for a number of hours equal to its creator's Stamina. Ghosts and other creatures of the Underworld can glut themselves on this rain, although they gain no Essence from it. Blood summoned with this spell rapidly mixes with dirt and clots into a stinking, sticky morass of polluted gore, wreaking havoc on the local environment. Most plants and smaller animals in the area affected die outright, while humans and other larger creatures must succeed in an hourly Stamina + Endurance check to avoid becoming violently ill and suffering a 1 die penalty to all actions. This spell -- and its concomitant scent of death -- also attracts hungry ghosts and other malevolent creatures for dozens of miles.
notes: Chapter Six: Necromancy, The Void Circle, pp. 228-229 (PDF 229-230). The source text's opening sentences about the blood droplets ('These droplets never fall to the earth. Instead, the rise and multiply...') read slightly garbled/grammatically inconsistent in the render; flagged for re-verification against a cleaner render, though the overall mechanic (blood ascends into a huge cloud, then falls as a corrosive/harmful downpour) is clear.

name: Dimming of the Light
summary: Void Circle spell; with this terrible spell, a necromancer can taint the divine Essence of a willing Solar, transforming him into the semblance of an Abyssal Exalt, requiring a ritual lasting from sunset to midnight and only performed in a shadowland or the Underworld.
requirements: Necromancy: Void Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: With this terrible spell, a necromancer can taint the divine Essence of a willing Solar, transforming him into the semblance of an Abyssal Exalt. This spell requires a ritual lasting from sunset to midnight and may only be cast within a shadowland or the Underworld. The Solar must willingly enter a Monstrance of Celestial Portion and only renounce his god and defile her Caste Mark by painting it with the blood of a murdered innocent. She then renounces her powers by one, cursing and foreswearing each Charm she knows. Lastly, she renounces her very name. Powerless, nameless, and empty, the broken Solar kneels and pledges her life and soul to the Malfeans and the Void. The necromancer stands by through this litany, silently praying for the dead Primordials to hear and affirm each renunciation in turn. At the final moment, on the stroke of midnight, the necromancer lays one hand on the forehead of the kneeling Solar and spends the required Essence. The animas of both characters immediately burst into full iconic splendor, shadow and light pressing fiercely against one another. Then, the Solar's anima begins to darken like a guttering candle, and at last dying as shadow swallow it for all time. When the necromancer withdraws his hand, her palm is slick with blood from the new Abyssal's Caste Mark. A Solar Exalted transformed in this manner gains a number of Abyssal Charms equal to the number of Solar Charms she knew before the change. She remembers all her spells, if any, though she can never again call on the magic of the Solar Circle. All magical items attuned to her former self follow her original caste, but they may be subsequently reattuned. Her new caste follows her original caste -- Dawn to Dusk, Zenith to Midnight, etc. Her Virtue Flaw vanishes, replaced with the Abyssal Curse. She is thereafter in all ways a deathknight and must contend with the advantages and disadvantages of her new state.
notes: Chapter Six: Necromancy, The Void Circle, p. 229 (PDF 230). This is the spell used by Deathlords to corrupt captured Solars into Abyssals; the source text's 'only renounce his god' phrasing reads slightly garbled, most likely intending 'must renounce his god'.

name: Inauspicious Citadel
summary: Void Circle spell; a necromancer can raise a fortress of gleaming obsidian and black basalt from the earth by first overseeing the excavation of a deep pit in the heart of a shadowland, then sacrificing at least 100 mortals down its depths before the ground shakes and the citadel rises fully formed and defensible.
requirements: Necromancy: Void Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: Through this spell, a necromancer can raise a fortress of gleaming obsidian and black basalt from the earth. Prior to casting the spell, the Exalt must oversee the excavation of a deep pit in the heart of a shadowland. This pit must be as wide as a man can reach with both arms outstretched and deep enough that a man holding a torch could not see the bottom if he peered into its depths. The Exalt then must sacrifice at least 100 mortals down its depths. Great care must be taken so that not even a single drop of blood falls anywhere but in the pit. After all the corpses have been thrown into the lightless shaft, the necromancer leans over the rim, spends the required Essence and cuts his hand. After one full breath level held the dripped into the dark, the ground shakes as the earth beneath the pit falls away to the depths of the Labyrinth and the dead gods reach slowly upward for the sacrifice. The necromancer and any bystanders have only a few minutes to flee the area before a castle of stone grinds up from beneath the pit. Although each citadel is unique, all emerge hollowed and defensible, with polished towers like jutting fingers of black stone inlaid with the meaningless mark marks of the Labyrinth. At the bottommost room of every citadel, lower than all its dungeons, a gleaming sanctuary of jet serves as a chapel to the Malfeans. In its center of its floor yawns an open shaft that extends down to the ultimate darkness and the whispering, dreaming gods that dwell there.
notes: Chapter Six: Necromancy, The Void Circle, p. 229 (PDF 230). A couple of the source sentences read slightly garbled in the render (e.g. 'After one full breath level held the dripped into the dark' and 'jutting fingers of black stone inlaid with the meaningless mark marks of the Labyrinth'); flagged for re-verification against a cleaner render, though the overall mechanic (mass mortal sacrifice into a pit raises an obsidian citadel) is clear.

name: Lord of the Dead
summary: Void Circle spell; upon casting, the necromancer's Caste Mark emerges glowing a baleful vivid red for the next full day, letting the character command any ghost, wraith, or undead creature of lower permanent Essence, though the spell cannot command or protect against other Abyssal Exalted or Deathlords.
requirements: Necromancy: Void Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: Upon casting this spell, the necromancer's Caste Mark emerges and glows a baleful vivid red for the next full day. While this light persists, the character may command any ghost, wraith, or undead creature that has lower permanent Essence than her own, and affected creatures must obey to the best of their abilities and intelligence. Commands can be as simple or complicated as desired, although zombies have difficulty comprehending anything more involved than a simple sentence. As a final benefit, no creature of death can attack the Exalt. This spell cannot command or protect against Abyssal Exalted or Deathlords.
notes: Chapter Six: Necromancy, The Void Circle, p. 229 (PDF 230).

name: Poisoning the Well
summary: Void Circle spell; through this spell, a necromancer can vastly speed the rate at which a Demesne changes its aspect to Abyssal, remaining at the heart of the Demesne, fasting and praying to the Malfeans for a number of days equal to its rating while the Essence powering the spell stays committed for the full duration.
requirements: Necromancy: Void Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: Through this spell, a necromancer can vastly speed the rate at which a Demesne changes its aspect to Abyssal. The Exalt must remain at the heart of the Demesne, fasting and praying to the Malfeans for a number of days equal to its rating. The Essence powering this spell must be spent at the beginning of this period and remains committed for the full duration. A Demesne polluted with this spell loses one point from its rating each month as the Underworld consumes its Essence. When the Demesne reaches a rating of zero, it shifts to an Abyssal aspect and begins to regain lost points until it returns to its original strength. A sorcerer who knows the spell Adamant Countermagic may arrest this decay by spending double the usual number of motes, but barring sorcerous or necromantic countermagic, no power short of an Incarna can halt the process. Should the corrosion be averted before it runs its course, lost points of strength return at the rate of one each year.
notes: Chapter Six: Necromancy, The Void Circle, p. 229 (PDF 230). Closes out the Void (Third) Circle spell list (Abyssal Aegis, Blood from the Slaughter [see Reaping the Fallen], Anguished Shade Harvest, Blood Monsoon, Dimming of the Light, Inauspicious Citadel, Lord of the Dead, Poisoning the Well -- 8 spells total) and, with it, the entire necromancy spell-list section of Chapter Six. Confirmed by the printed folio '229' visible at the bottom of the rendered PDF page 230; the next PDF pages (231 full-page illustration, 232 short-fiction interlude) precede the real 'CHAPTER SIX: THE ARTS OF THE DEAD' title page at printed p. 232 (PDF 233), which covers the Crafts of the Dead (Necrosurgery/Jadecrafting/Soulforging/Moliation/Pandemonium) rather than any further necromancy spells.

name: Craft (Moliation)
summary: One of the Crafts of the Dead: by developing this Ability, a ghost learns the subtle techniques of working the wraithly corpus, shaping and modifying the stuff of his own ghostly form from gossamer-delicate feathers to gleaming armor; used only by the dead, not by living Abyssals.
requirements: Craft Ability framework/specialty rules; not itself a selectable Charm.
mechanics: By developing this Ability, the ghost learns the subtle techniques of working the wraithly corpus. This knowledge allows the ghost to shape, mold and modify the stuff that makes up his form, to, from gossamer-delicate feathers to gleaming armor. The natural laws of living Creation have no sway in the Underworld, and the substance of a ghost can take form a skilled master of Moliation wishes it to, from gossamer-delicate feathers to gleaming armor. Moliation does not grant the ability to reshape ghostly ectoplasm. Rather, it provides the knowledge that a ghost with these powers needs to use them to good effect. Ghosts who are familiar with Moliation can detect its use on others, and they can guide others in its use (-1 difficulty on rolls involving Moliation for ghosts being advised by another with a higher level of the Ability). Moliation does not grant knowledge of soul-forging. Specialties: Masks, Monstrous Forms, Weaponry, Armor, Disguise. Standard: Detect the use of Moliation on others, add or remove a feature crudely, create a lifelike mask. Challenging: Create a mask that inspires fear, create useful weaponry, craft a ghost into a new shape. Legendary: Reshape a ghost into an armored killing machine. Create masks so lifelike that none may recognize the ghost's true appearance.
notes: Chapter Six: The Arts of the Dead, 'The Crafts of the Dead' section, first of the four ghost-usable Crafts detailed, p. 232 (PDF 233). Per the source, only ghosts (not living Abyssal Exalted) can learn Moliation.

name: Craft (Pandemonium)
summary: One of the Crafts of the Dead: the art of crafting horrors, illusions and nightmares, and also of making dreams and fantasies, rendering it one of the most versatile ghostly crafts; used only by the dead, not by living Abyssals.
requirements: Craft Ability framework/specialty rules; not itself a selectable Charm.
mechanics: Pandemonium is the art of crafting horrors, illusions and nightmares. It is also the art of making dreams and fantasies, rendering it one of the most versatile of the ghostly crafts. Improving one's knowledge of Pandemonium improves one's ability to craft illusions of all sorts, from the magnificent to the soul-rending. The best exemplars of the craft, of course, are able to do both, but most of its practitioners have their own specialties. Pandemonium does not grant the ability to shape dreams, illusions and so forth. Instead, it is merely the knowledge of how to do so. A ghost with innate talent but no knowledge of Pandemonium can still summon forth horrors, but a master of Craft (Pandemonium) with no innate Arcanoi is left commenting on the works of others. Specialties: Insects, Ichors, Scuttling Things, Shapeless Horrors, Fantasies, Phantom Epics. Standard: Detect another's use of Pandemonium, create a simple illusion, affect the living world. Challenging: Create a complex illusion involving more than one sense, manifest a horror of some sort, engage in strenuous poltergeist activity. Legendary: A flood of devouring beetles and locusts, reaching into the Mouth of Oblivion.
notes: Chapter Six: The Arts of the Dead, 'The Crafts of the Dead' section, second of the four ghost-usable Crafts detailed, p. 233 (PDF 234). Per the source, only ghosts (not living Abyssal Exalted) can learn Pandemonium.

name: Craft (Soulforging)
summary: One of the Crafts of the Dead: the art of hammering the ghostly flesh of the dead into the useful implements of the Underworld, also allowing the creation of soulsteel by combining ectoplasm with the ores of the Labyrinth; usable by both ghosts and living Abyssal Exalted.
requirements: Craft Ability framework/specialty rules; not itself a selectable Charm.
mechanics: Soulforging is the art of hammering the ghostly flesh of the dead into the useful implements of the Underworld. It is also the art that allows the creation of soulsteel that combines ectoplasm with the ores of the Labyrinth. While superficially soulforging resembles mortal smithing, it has demands and requirements that living blacksmiths never dreamed of. For one thing, the material of the smith does not scream while it is under the hammer. For another, the dangers of working with flames of pure Essence are far, far greater than any perils a mere mortal forge can pose. Without the proper equipment, soulforging is mostly useless. While it does grant any ghost who possesses the analytical eye to identify soulforged work and an understanding of the process by which souls are transformed into commodities, it is primarily an active skill. Full usage of Craft (Soulforging) requires a smith's setup -- an anvil, a hammer, an Essence forge and, most importantly, a supply of souls. Soulforgers prefer equipment made of soulsteel or jade when they can get it -- the relentless heat and pounding tends to reduce lesser equipment to rubble in short order. However, in a pinch they'll take whatever they can get, so long as they have the raw materials they need. Specialties: Objets d'Art, Weaponry, Armor, Construction. Standard: Identify soulforged objects, render a soul into raw materials, make a basic sword or other simple item, create sturdy items for use in construction in the Underworld. Challenging: Create a unique weapon, build a device with multiple moving parts out of soulforged elements, create a flexible chain, create a soulforged item that can use Essence. Legendary: Construct a soulforged automaton, make a unique weapon, do jewelry filigree work, create and work with soulsteel.
compatibility: Usable by both ghosts and living Abyssal Exalted, per the Useful Crafts summary (unlike Moliation and Pandemonium, which are ghost-only).
notes: Chapter Six: The Arts of the Dead, 'The Crafts of the Dead' section, third of the four Crafts detailed, pp. 233-234 (PDF 234-235).

name: Craft (Jadecrafting)
summary: One of the Crafts of the Dead: the last of the materials the artisans of the dead work with is jade, potent in the living but even more special in the lands of the dead, though too fragile to be Moliated; usable by both ghosts and living Abyssal Exalted.
requirements: Craft Ability framework/specialty rules; not itself a selectable Charm.
mechanics: The last of the materials the artisans of the dead work with is jade. Potent in the lands of the living, it becomes even more special in the lands of the dead. Too fragile to be Moliated, jade is nevertheless extraordinarily valuable to the Restless Dead, and those who can work it are highly regarded. Specialties: Grave Goods, Jewelry, Ornamental Weaponry, Magical Artifacts. Standard: Take a grave good and render it useful in the Underworld, carve raw jade into a useful shape, evaluate the worth of a jade item. Challenging: Create useful jade implements, devices and chains, incorporate jade into a device created in the Underworld. Legendary: Craft jade jewelry pleasing to one of the Deathlords, infuse a jade item with Essence.
compatibility: Usable by both ghosts and living Abyssal Exalted, per the Useful Crafts summary (unlike Moliation and Pandemonium, which are ghost-only).
notes: Chapter Six: The Arts of the Dead, 'The Crafts of the Dead' section, last of the four Crafts detailed, p. 234 (PDF 235). Immediately followed by a 'Soulforging and Jadecrafting' sidebar noting both crafts follow The Book of Three Circles pp. 88-89 rules, substituting Dexterity + Craft (Soulforging) or Craft (Jadecrafting) for Intelligence + Occult on Step Three: Creation rolls, and that forging artifacts requires exotic ingredients often found only within the Labyrinth. Craft (Necrosurgery) -- the fifth Craft named in the Chapter Four 'Useful Crafts' summary -- is NOT detailed in this section: per that summary it is used only by living Abyssal Exalted, not by ghosts, and this ghost-focused 'Arts of the Dead' chapter does not give it its own specialties/Standard/Challenging/Legendary write-up. Its only mechanical detail found in this book remains via the Walking War Machine necromancy spell and the Medicine Charm Bone Graft Technique (both already inventoried); no separate Necrosurgery framework block was located after checking pp. 232-235.

name: Abyssal-Specific Merits/Flaws (confirmed absent)
summary: This book does not contain a distinct Merits/Flaws section or any Abyssal-specific Merits or Flaws beyond the standard Exalted core-book set; confirmed by a chapter-by-chapter check and by the printed character sheet, which has no Merits/Flaws fields at all.
requirements: N/A -- documents a negative finding, not a selectable power.
mechanics: No chapter of this book (One through Seven) contains a section titled 'Merits' or 'Flaws' or any equivalent framework of Abyssal-specific advantages/disadvantages purchased with bonus points, distinct from the standard Virtue Flaw/Abyssal Curse system (already inventoried) and the standard Exalted core-book Merits and Flaws list. Chapter Four (Traits) covers Attributes, Abilities, Backgrounds (including the new/altered Abyssal-specific ones, already inventoried), Charms, Virtues, Willpower, and Essence, with no Merits/Flaws subsection. Chapter Five is entirely Charms. Chapter Six covers necromancy spells and the ghost-only Crafts/Arcanoi framework (Six Demon Bag, Mortal-Shadowing Technique, Puppeteer's Masterful Hand, etc. -- all ghost powers, not player-facing Merits/Flaws). Chapter Seven ('Storytelling', beginning p. 264/PDF 265) is Storyteller-facing advice about Deathlords and sample series, not character-creation mechanics. Most decisively, the book's own printed character sheet (pp. 288 and 291, PDF 289 and 292) lists Attributes, Abilities, Backgrounds, Charms, Weapons, Willpower, Virtues, Anima, Health, Resonance, Resonance Effects, and Essence -- but has no Merits or Flaws fields whatsoever, confirming the designers did not intend a distinct Abyssal Merits/Flaws framework for this book.
compatibility: Standard Exalted core-book Merits and Flaws remain available to Abyssal characters at Storyteller discretion, as for any Exalted splat; this book adds none of its own.
notes: Checked across Chapters One through Seven and the printed character sheet (pp. 288, 291 / PDF 289, 292); no Abyssal-specific Merits/Flaws section exists in this book. This closes out scope item 4 from this inventory pass as a confirmed-absent finding rather than a further gap.
